title.zh: 卷一百五十五 列傳第一百〇四: 穆寧 崔邠 竇群 李遜 薛戎
title.en: Volume 155 Biographies 105: Mu Ning, Cui Bin, Dou Qun, Li Xun, Xue Rong
title.raw: 卷一百五十五 列傳第一百〇四: 穆寧 崔邠 竇群 李遜 薛戎 Volume 155 Biographies 105: Mu Ning, Cui Bin, Dou Qun, Li Xun, Xue Rong

sentences.zh: 穆寧，懷州河內人也。

translations.literal: Mu Ning was a native of Henei in Huai Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Mu Ning was from Henei in Huai Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父元休，以文學著。

translations.literal: His father Yu Xiu was renowned for literary learning.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yu Xiu was known for his scholarship.

sentences.zh: 撰《洪範外傳》十篇，開元中獻之。

translations.literal: He composed ten chapters of the Outer Commentary on the Great Plan and presented it in the Kaiyuan era.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote ten chapters of an Outer Commentary on the Great Plan and presented the work to the throne during the Kaiyuan reign.

sentences.zh: 玄宗賜帛，授偃師縣丞、安陽令。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong bestowed silk and appointed him Assistant Magistrate of Yanshi County and Magistrate of Anyang.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong rewarded him with silk and appointed him assistant magistrate of Yanshi and magistrate of Anyang.

sentences.zh: 寧清慎剛正，重交遊，以氣節自任。

translations.literal: Ning was pure, cautious, upright, and firm; he valued friendships and held himself to moral integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Ning was upright, principled, and fastidious in conduct; he prized friendship and measured himself by personal integrity.

sentences.zh: 少以明經調授鹽山尉。

translations.literal: In his youth he passed the Examination on the Classics and was transferred to serve as Wei of Yanshan.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man he qualified in the classics examination and was posted as district defender of Yanshan.

sentences.zh: 是時，安祿山始叛，偽署劉道玄為景城守，寧唱義起兵，斬道玄首。

translations.literal: At that time An Lushan had just rebelled and had falsely appointed Liu Daoxuan as defender of Jingcheng. Ning raised troops in righteous cause and beheaded Daoxuan.
translations.idiomatic: At that time An Lushan had just risen in rebellion and installed Liu Daoxuan as pretender defender of Jingcheng. Ning rallied loyal forces and beheaded Daoxuan.

sentences.zh: 傳檄郡邑，多有應者。

translations.literal: He circulated proclamations through the counties and cities, and many responded.
translations.idiomatic: His call to arms spread through the neighboring prefectures, and many answered it.

sentences.zh: 賊將史思明來寇郡，寧以攝東光令將兵禦之。

translations.literal: The rebel general Shi Siming came to attack the commandery. Ning, acting as provisional magistrate of Dongguang, led troops to resist him.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebel general Shi Siming invaded the commandery, Ning took command as acting magistrate of Dongguang and marched out to meet him.

sentences.zh: 思明遣使說誘，寧立斬之。

translations.literal: Siming sent an envoy to persuade and entice him. Ning at once beheaded the envoy.
translations.idiomatic: Siming sent envoys to win him over; Ning had them executed on the spot.

sentences.zh: 郡懼賊怨深，後大兵至，奪寧兵及攝縣。

translations.literal: The commandery feared that the rebels would bear deep resentment. Later, when a large army arrived, it stripped Ning of his troops and his acting magistracy.
translations.idiomatic: The commandery authorities, afraid of provoking the rebels further, later stripped Ning of his forces and his acting post when imperial troops arrived.

sentences.zh: 初，寧佐采訪使巡按，常過平原，與太守顏真卿密揣祿山必叛。

translations.literal: Earlier, while assisting a touring commissioner on inspection rounds, Ning often passed through Pingyuan and with the prefect Yan Zhenqing secretly inferred that Lushan would certainly rebel.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while serving as aide to a regional inspection commissioner, Ning had often passed through Pingyuan and confided in the prefect Yan Zhenqing that Lushan was sure to rebel.

sentences.zh: 至是，真卿亦唱義，舉郡兵以拒祿山。

translations.literal: At this juncture Zhenqing also raised righteous troops and mustered the commandery forces to resist Lushan.
translations.idiomatic: By then Zhenqing too had taken up arms and mobilized the commandery to resist Lushan.

sentences.zh: 會間使持書遺真卿曰：「夫子為衛君乎？」

translations.literal: It happened that an envoy came bearing a letter to Zhenqing saying: "Will the Master be like the gentleman of Wei?"
translations.idiomatic: An envoy arrived with a message for Zhenqing: "Will you not act like the gentleman of Wei?"

sentences.zh: 更無他詞。

translations.literal: There was nothing more in the message.
translations.idiomatic: The letter said nothing else.

sentences.zh: 真卿得書大喜，因奏署大理評事、河北采訪支使。

translations.literal: When Zhenqing received the letter he was greatly pleased and thereupon memorialized to appoint [Ning] as evaluative official of the Court of Judicial Review and assistant touring commissioner of Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenqing was overjoyed and promptly had Ning appointed judicial reviewer and assistant Hebei touring commissioner.

sentences.zh: 寧以長子屬母弟曰：「惟爾所適，茍不乏嗣，吾無累矣。」

translations.literal: Ning entrusted his eldest son to his younger brother by the mother's side, saying: "You may do with him as you see fit. So long as our line is not cut off, I have no further burden."
translations.idiomatic: Ning placed his eldest son in his uterine younger brother's care, saying: "Do with him as you think best. If our line is not lost, I have nothing left to weigh me down."

sentences.zh: 因往平原，謂真卿曰：「先人有嗣矣！

translations.literal: He then went to Pingyuan and said to Zhenqing: "Our forebears have an heir now!
translations.idiomatic: He went on to Pingyuan and told Zhenqing: "The ancestors already have their heir.

sentences.zh: 古所謂死有輕於鴻毛者，寧是也。

translations.literal: As the ancients said, there are deaths lighter than a goose feather — such is what Ning has done.
translations.idiomatic: The ancients spoke of deaths lighter than a goose feather — this is the kind of death I choose.

sentences.zh: 願佐公以定危難。」

translations.literal: I wish to assist you, sir, in settling this peril."
translations.idiomatic: I wish to serve under you and help bring an end to this crisis."

sentences.zh: 真卿深然之。

translations.literal: Zhenqing strongly approved of this.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenqing heartily agreed.

sentences.zh: 其後，寧計或不行，真卿迫蹙，棄郡，夜渡河而南，見肅宗於鳳翔。

translations.literal: Afterwards Ning's plans were not always followed. Zhenqing was pressed hard, abandoned the commandery, crossed the river by night heading south, and met Emperor Suzong at Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Ning's counsel was not always heeded, Zhenqing came under pressure, gave up the commandery, crossed the river by night to the south, and presented himself to Emperor Suzong at Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 帝問拒賊之狀，真卿曰：「臣不用穆寧之言，功業不成。」

translations.literal: The Emperor asked about resisting the rebels. Zhenqing said: "Had your subject not used Mu Ning's counsel, his achievements would not have been realized."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked how he had resisted the rebels. Zhenqing replied: "Had I not followed Mu Ning's advice, I would have accomplished nothing."

sentences.zh: 帝奇之，發驛召寧，將以右職待之。

translations.literal: The Emperor was struck by this and dispatched a courier to summon Ning, intending to treat him with a high office.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was impressed and sent a fast courier to summon Ning, intending to reward him with a senior post.

sentences.zh: 會真卿以抗直失旨，事遂止。

translations.literal: But then Zhenqing lost favor for his blunt integrity, and the matter came to nothing.
translations.idiomatic: But Zhenqing soon fell from favor for his outspoken integrity, and the appointment never went through.

sentences.zh: 上元二年，累官至殿中侍御史，佐鹽鐵轉運使。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shangyuan he had risen through repeated promotions to Palace Attendant Within the Hall, assisting the salt-iron transport commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: By the second year of Shangyuan he had risen to palace attendant censor and was assisting the salt and iron transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 副元帥李光弼以餉運不繼，或惡寧者，誣譖於光弼，光弼揚言欲殺寧。

translations.literal: The deputy commander Li Guangbi, because grain supplies were not reaching the army in time, was slandered by those who disliked Ning, who misrepresented him to Guangbi. Guangbi openly declared he would kill Ning.
translations.idiomatic: Because supplies were not reaching the army on time, those who bore Ning a grudge slandered him to the deputy commander Li Guangbi, who openly threatened to have Ning executed.

sentences.zh: 寧直抵徐州見光弼，喻以大義，不為撓折。

translations.literal: Ning went straight to Xuzhou to see Guangbi, expounded the greater principle, and was not cowed.
translations.idiomatic: Ning went straight to Xuzhou to confront Guangbi, set forth the larger cause, and would not be intimidated.

sentences.zh: 光弼深重之，寧得行其職。

translations.literal: Guangbi came to esteem him deeply, and Ning was able to carry out his duties.
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi came to respect him deeply, and Ning was able to carry out his duties.

sentences.zh: 寶應初，轉侍御史，為河南轉運租庸鹽鐵等副使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Baoying he was transferred to regular attendant censor and made vice commissioner of Henan transport for rent, corvée, salt, and iron.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Baoying era he became regular attendant censor and vice commissioner of Henan transport for rent, corvée, salt, and iron.

sentences.zh: 明年，遷戶部員外郎。

translations.literal: The next year he was promoted to vice director of the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was promoted to vice director of the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 無幾，加兼御史中丞，為河南、江南轉運使。

translations.literal: Before long he was additionally made vice censor-in-chief and Henan and Jiangnan transport commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was also made vice censor-in-chief and commissioner of transport for Henan and Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 廣德初，加庫部郎中。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Guangde he was further made director of the treasury bureau in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Guangde era he was further appointed director of the treasury bureau.

sentences.zh: 是時河運不通，漕挽由漢、沔自商山達京師。

translations.literal: At that time transport on the Yellow River was cut off, and haulage went by the Han and Mian rivers from Shangshan to reach the capital.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Grand Canal was blocked, and grain was hauled along the Han and Mian rivers from Shangshan to the capital.

sentences.zh: 選鎮夏口者，詔以寧為鄂州刺史、鄂嶽沔都團練使，及淮西鄂嶽租庸鹽鐵沿江轉運使，賜金紫。

translations.literal: When it was decided to station a defense at Xiakou, an edict appointed Ning prefect of Ezhou, commander-in-chief of E, Yue, and Mian, and commissioner for Huai-Xi, E, and Yue rent, corvée, salt, iron, and transport along the river—granting him the gold-purple insignia.
translations.idiomatic: When the court chose to fortify Xiakou, an edict made Ning prefect of Ezhou, regional commander of E, Yue, and Mian, and commissioner for Huai-Xi and E-Yue rent, corvée, salt, iron, and river transport, with the gold-and-purple insignia.

sentences.zh: 時淮西節度使李忠臣貪暴不奉法，設防戍以稅商賈，又縱兵士剽劫，行人殆絕。

translations.literal: At that time the Huai-Xi military governor Li Zhongchen was greedy and violent and did not obey the law. He set guard posts to tax merchants and also allowed his soldiers to plunder, so that travelers nearly vanished.
translations.idiomatic: The Huai-Xi military governor Li Zhongchen was greedy, violent, and lawless; he set checkpoints to tax merchants and let his troops plunder until travelers all but disappeared.

sentences.zh: 與寧夾淮為理，憚寧威名，寇盜輒止。

translations.literal: He and Ning administered on opposite banks of the Huai. Zhongchen feared Ning's reputation, and bandits at once ceased.
translations.idiomatic: He and Ning governed on opposite banks of the Huai. Zhongchen feared Ning's reputation, and banditry promptly ceased.

sentences.zh: 沔州別駕薛彥偉坐事忤旨，寧仗之致死。

translations.literal: The Mianzhou vice prefect Xue Yanwei offended the throne in a case; Ning beat him to death with staves.
translations.idiomatic: The Mianzhou vice prefect Xue Yanwei had offended the throne in a case; Ning had him beaten to death with staves.

sentences.zh: 寧坐貶虔州司馬，重貶昭州平集尉。

translations.literal: Ning was sentenced to demotion to Qianzhou army adjutant, then further demoted to registrar of Pingji in Shaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ning was demoted to army adjutant of Qianzhou, then further demoted to registrar of Pingji in Shaozhou.

sentences.zh: 大歷四年，起授監察御史，領轉運留後事於淄青。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Dali he was recalled and appointed investigating censor, taking charge of transport rear-office affairs in Ziqing.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Dali he was recalled as investigating censor and placed in charge of transport rear-office affairs in Ziqing.

sentences.zh: 間一年，改檢校司封郎中、兼侍御史，領轉運留後事於江西。

translations.literal: A year later he was changed to acting director of the bureau of honors and also regular attendant censor, managing transport rear-office affairs in Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he became acting director of the bureau of honors and regular attendant censor, overseeing transport rear-office affairs in Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 明年，拜檢校秘書少監，兼和州刺史，理有善政。

translations.literal: The next year he was appointed acting vice director of the Secretariat and concurrently prefect of Hezhou, governing with notable good policies.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was appointed acting vice director of the Secretariat and concurrently prefect of Hezhou, where his administration won praise.

sentences.zh: 居無何，官罷。

translations.literal: Before long his office was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was removed from office.

sentences.zh: 代寧者以天寶版籍校見戶，誣以逋亡多，坐貶泉州司戶。

translations.literal: His successor compared household registers against the Tianbao census and falsely charged many absconded households; on this Ning was demoted to registrar of Quanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His successor compared the current registers with the Tianbao census and falsely claimed a large number of missing households; on this charge Ning was demoted to registrar of Quanzhou.

sentences.zh: 寧子贊，守闕三年告冤。

translations.literal: Ning's son Zan waited at the palace gates three years to proclaim his father's injustice.
translations.idiomatic: Ning's son Zan waited at the palace gates for three years to plead his father's innocence.

sentences.zh: 詔遣御史按覆，而人戶增倍，詔書召寧，除右諭德。

translations.literal: An edict sent a censor to investigate. The registered households had in fact doubled. An edict summoned Ning and appointed him right remonstrator of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: An edict sent a censor to reinvestigate the case; the registered households had in fact doubled. Ning was summoned and appointed right remonstrator of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 寧強毅，不能事權貴。

translations.literal: Ning was forceful and could not serve the powerful.
translations.idiomatic: Ning was forceful and would not court the powerful.

sentences.zh: 執政者以為不附己，且憚其難制，故處之散位。

translations.literal: Those in power thought him not attached to themselves and also feared he would be hard to control, so they kept him in dispersed offices.
translations.idiomatic: Those in power regarded him as not on their side and feared he would be hard to control, so they kept him in honorific posts without real authority.

sentences.zh: 寧默默不得誌，且曰：「時不我容，我不時殉，則非吾之進也，在於退乎！」

translations.literal: Ning bore his frustration in silence and said: "If the times will not accept me, and I do not sacrifice myself to the times, then advancing is not my path—is withdrawal perhaps the answer?"
translations.idiomatic: Ning bore his frustration in silence and said: "If the times will not have me, and I do not throw myself away for the times, then advancement is not my way—is withdrawal perhaps the answer?"

sentences.zh: 辭病居家，請告幾十旬者數矣。

translations.literal: He pleaded illness and stayed home, requesting leave for scores of days several times.
translations.idiomatic: He pleaded illness and stayed home, requesting leave for months on end several times.

sentences.zh: 親友強之，復一朝請。

translations.literal: Friends and kin urged him, and he attended court once more.
translations.idiomatic: Friends and relatives pressed him, and he returned to court once more.

sentences.zh: 上居奉天，寧詣行在，拜秘書少監。

translations.literal: When the Emperor was at Fengtian, Ning went to the traveling palace and was appointed vice director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor was at Fengtian, Ning went to the traveling court and was appointed vice director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 興元初，改右庶子。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xingyuan he was changed to right vice guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Xingyuan era he was made right vice guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 德宗還京師，寧曰：「可以行吾誌矣。」

translations.literal: When Dezong returned to the capital, Ning said: "I can now carry out my resolve."
translations.idiomatic: When Dezong returned to the capital, Ning said: "I can now live by my principles."

sentences.zh: 因移病，罷歸東都。

translations.literal: He therefore pleaded transfer for illness and retired to the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: He then pleaded illness, resigned, and returned to the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 貞元六年，就拜秘書監致仕。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Zhenyuan he accepted appointment as director of the Secretariat with permission to retire.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Zhenyuan he accepted appointment as director of the Secretariat and retired from office.

sentences.zh: 寧好學，善教諸子，家道以嚴稱。

translations.literal: Ning loved learning and taught his sons well; his household was known for strictness.
translations.idiomatic: Ning loved learning and taught his sons well; his household was known for its strict discipline.

sentences.zh: 事寡姊以悌聞。

translations.literal: He served his widowed elder sister with filial devotion that was widely heard.
translations.idiomatic: His devotion to his widowed elder sister was renowned.

sentences.zh: 通達體命，未嘗服藥。

translations.literal: He understood the principles of fate and never took medicine.
translations.idiomatic: He understood the workings of fate and never took medicine.

sentences.zh: 每誡諸子曰：「吾聞君子之事親，養誌為大，直道而已。

translations.literal: He often admonished his sons: "I have heard that in serving parents, the noble son nourishes their will—straightforward conduct alone.
translations.idiomatic: He often warned his sons: "I have heard that in serving one's parents, the greatest thing is to honor their will—nothing but the straight path.

sentences.zh: 慎無為諂，吾之誌也。」

translations.literal: Take care never to flatter—that is my resolve."
translations.idiomatic: Take care never to flatter—that is my resolve."

sentences.zh: 貞元十年十月卒，時年七十九。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the tenth year of Zhenyuan he died, aged seventy-nine.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the tenth year of Zhenyuan he died at the age of seventy-nine.

sentences.zh: 四子：贊、質、員、賞。

translations.literal: He had four sons: Zan, Zhi, Yuan, and Shang.
translations.idiomatic: He had four sons: Zan, Zhi, Yuan, and Shang.

sentences.zh: 贊，字相明，釋褐為濟源主簿。

translations.literal: Zan, courtesy name Xiangming, entered service upon leaving the russet as recorder of Jiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Zan, whose courtesy name was Xiangming, began his career as recorder of Jiyuan upon leaving the russet.

sentences.zh: 時父寧為和州刺史，以剛直不屈於廉使，遂被誣奏，貶泉州司戶參軍。

translations.literal: At that time his father Ning was prefect of Hezhou. Because he was upright and would not yield to the fiscal commissioner, he was slandered in a memorial and demoted to army adjutant of Quanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At that time his father Ning was prefect of Hezhou. Because he was upright and refused to yield to the fiscal commissioner, he was slandered in a memorial and demoted to army adjutant of Quanzhou.

sentences.zh: 贊奔赴闕庭，號泣上訴。

translations.literal: Zan raced to the imperial court, weeping and appealing above.
translations.idiomatic: Zan rushed to the capital, weeping as he appealed to the throne.

sentences.zh: 詔御史覆問，寧方得雪。

translations.literal: An edict sent a censor to re-examine the case, and Ning was cleared.
translations.idiomatic: An edict sent a censor to reinvestigate, and Ning was cleared.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「令子申父之冤，憲臣奉君之命，楚劍不沖於牛鬥，秦臺自洗於塵埃。」

translations.literal: An edict said: "The worthy son proclaims his father's wrong; the disciplinary official carries out the sovereign's command. The Chu sword never strikes the Ox and Hare stars; the Qin terrace washes itself clean of dust."
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared: "The worthy son vindicates his father's wrong; the disciplinary official carries out the sovereign's command. The Chu sword never strikes the Ox and Hare stars; the Qin terrace washes itself clean of dust."

sentences.zh: 由是知名。

translations.literal: From this he became well known.
translations.idiomatic: From this he became widely known.

sentences.zh: 累遷京兆兵曹參軍、殿中侍御史，轉侍御史，分司東都。

translations.literal: He rose through Jingzhao army adjutant, palace attendant censor within the hall, regular attendant censor, and commissioner at the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through Jingzhao army adjutant, palace attendant censor, regular attendant censor, and commissioner at the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 時陜州觀察使盧嶽妾裴氏，以有子，嶽妻分財不及，訴於官，贊鞫其事。

translations.literal: At that time the Shaanzhou observer Lu Yue's concubine Lady Pei, because she had borne a son, had not received a share of the estate when Yue's wife divided the property. She sued at court. Zan judged the case.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Shaanzhou observer Lu Yue's concubine Lady Pei, who had borne a son, had been left out when Yue's wife divided the estate. She brought suit, and Zan heard the case.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞盧佋佐之，令深繩裴罪。

translations.literal: The vice censor-in-chief Lu Bian supported him and ordered that Pei's offense be punished severely.
translations.idiomatic: The vice censor-in-chief Lu Bian backed him and ordered that Pei be punished to the full extent of the law.

sentences.zh: 贊持平不許。

translations.literal: Zan held to fairness and would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Zan held to fairness and would not allow it.

sentences.zh: 宰臣竇參與佋善，參、佋俱持權，怒贊以小事不受指使，遂下贊獄。

translations.literal: The chief minister Dou Can was friendly with Bian. Can and Bian both held power and, angry that Zan on a minor matter would not follow their orders, had Zan thrown into prison.
translations.idiomatic: The chief minister Dou Can was on good terms with Bian. Can and Bian both held power and, angry that Zan would not follow their orders in a minor matter, had him thrown into prison.

sentences.zh: 侍御史杜倫希其意，誣贊受裴之金，鞭其使以成其獄，甚急。

translations.literal: The attendant censor Du Lun guessed their intent, falsely charged that Zan had taken gold from Pei, and flogged his envoy to complete the case—most urgent.
translations.idiomatic: The attendant censor Du Lun guessed their intent, falsely charged that Zan had taken bribes from Pei, and flogged his messenger to force a confession—the case was pressed urgently.

sentences.zh: 贊弟賞，馳詣闕，撾登聞鼓。

translations.literal: Zan's younger brother Shang galloped to the palace and struck the petition drum.
translations.idiomatic: Zan's younger brother Shang galloped to the palace and struck the petition drum.

sentences.zh: 詔三司使覆理無驗，出為郴州刺史。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the three offices to re-examine; no proof was found, and he was sent out as prefect of Chenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the three judicial offices to reinvestigate; finding no evidence, they sent him out as prefect of Chenzhou.

sentences.zh: 參敗，征拜刑部郎中。

translations.literal: When Can fell, Zan was summoned and appointed director of the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: When Can fell from power, Zan was summoned and appointed director of the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 因次對，德宗嘉其才，擢為御史中丞。

translations.literal: On a subsequent audience Dezong praised his talent and promoted him to vice censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: On a subsequent audience Dezong praised his talent and promoted him to vice censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 時裴延齡判度支，以奸巧承恩。

translations.literal: At that time Pei Yanling oversaw the Treasury; he curried favor with cunning.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Pei Yanling oversaw the Treasury and curried favor through cunning.

sentences.zh: 屬吏有贓犯，贊鞫理承伏。

translations.literal: When a subordinate committed a graft offense, Zan tried the case and obtained confession.
translations.idiomatic: When a subordinate committed graft, Zan tried the case and obtained a confession.

sentences.zh: 延齡請曲法出之，贊三執不許，以款狀聞。

translations.literal: Yanling asked that the law be bent to release him. Three times Zan refused and reported the confession to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Yanling asked that the law be bent to release him. Three times Zan refused and reported the confession to the throne.

sentences.zh: 延齡誣贊不平，貶饒州別駕。

translations.literal: Yanling slandered Zan as partial and had him demoted to vice prefect of Raozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yanling slandered Zan as biased and had him demoted to vice prefect of Raozhou.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂，再轉虔、常二州刺史。

translations.literal: On mourning for his mother he was transferred in turn to prefect of Qian and Chang.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning for his mother he served in turn as prefect of Qian and Chang.

sentences.zh: 憲宗即位，拜宣州刺史、御史中丞，充宣歙觀察使，所蒞皆有政聲。

translations.literal: When Xianzong took the throne, Zan was appointed prefect of Xuanzhou and vice censor-in-chief, made Xuan-She observer; everywhere he served he earned praise for good governance.
translations.idiomatic: When Xianzong took the throne, Zan was appointed prefect of Xuanzhou and vice censor-in-chief and made Xuan-She observer; everywhere he served he won praise for good governance.

sentences.zh: 永貞元年十一月卒，時年五十八，贈工部尚書。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the first year of Yongzhen he died, aged fifty-eight. He was posthumously made minister of works.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the first year of Yongzhen he died at the age of fifty-eight. He was posthumously made minister of works.

sentences.zh: 贊與弟質、員、賞以家行人材為搢紳所仰。

translations.literal: Zan and his brothers Zhi, Yuan, and Shang were admired among the gentry for their family conduct and personal ability.
translations.idiomatic: Zan and his brothers Zhi, Yuan, and Shang were admired among the gentry for their family conduct and personal ability.

sentences.zh: 贊官達，父母尚無恙，家法清嚴。

translations.literal: Though Zan had risen high, his parents were still alive, and the household rules remained strict.
translations.idiomatic: Though Zan had risen high in office, his parents were still alive, and the household rules remained strict.

sentences.zh: 贊兄弟奉指使，笞責如僮仆，贊最孝謹。

translations.literal: The Zan brothers obeyed their father's orders; he beat and reprimanded them like servants. Zan was the most filial and careful.
translations.idiomatic: The Zan brothers obeyed their father's orders; he beat and reprimanded them like servants. Zan was the most filial and careful.

sentences.zh: 質強直，應制策入第三等。

translations.literal: Zhi was forceful and upright; in the palace examination policy essay he placed in the third grade.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi was forceful and upright; in the palace examination policy essay he placed in the third grade.

sentences.zh: 其所條對，至今傳之。

translations.literal: His answers are still transmitted today.
translations.idiomatic: His answers are still read today.

sentences.zh: 自補闕至給事中，時政得失，未嘗不先論諫。

translations.literal: From remonstrator to petitioner he never failed to speak first on the gains and losses of current policy.
translations.idiomatic: From remonstrator to petitioner he was always the first to speak on the rights and wrongs of current policy.

sentences.zh: 元和初，掌賦使院多擅禁系戶人，而有笞掠至死者。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanhe the salt monopoly office often exceeded its authority in confining registered households, and some were beaten to death.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Yuanhe era the salt monopoly office often exceeded its authority in detaining registered households, and some were beaten to death.

sentences.zh: 質乃論奏鹽鐵轉運司應決私鹽，系囚須與州府長吏監決。

translations.literal: Zhi memorialized that the Salt and Iron Transport Commission, when punishing private salt offenders, must have the prefectural chief official oversee the punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi memorialized that when the Salt and Iron Transport Commission punished private salt offenders, the prefectural chief official must oversee the punishment.

sentences.zh: 自是刑名畫一。

translations.literal: From then on penal procedure was unified.
translations.idiomatic: From then on penal procedure was standardized.

sentences.zh: 憲宗以王承宗叛，用內官吐突承璀為招討使。

translations.literal: Because Chengzong of Hengjie rebelled, the emperor employed the inner eunuch Tuoba Chenghui as pacification commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Chengzong rebelled, Xianzong appointed the inner eunuch Tuoba Chenghui as pacification commissioner.

sentences.zh: 質率同列伏閣論奏，言自古無以中官為將帥者。

translations.literal: Zhi led his colleagues in kneeling at the palace gate to remonstrate, declaring that since antiquity there had never been an inner eunuch as commander.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi led his colleagues in kneeling at the palace gate to remonstrate, declaring that since antiquity there had never been an inner eunuch as military commander.

sentences.zh: 上雖改其名，心頗不悅，尋改質為太子左庶子。

translations.literal: Though the emperor changed the title, he was quite displeased and soon moved Zhi to left vice guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Though the emperor changed the title, he was displeased and soon transferred Zhi to left vice guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 五年，坐與楊憑善，出為開州刺史。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was punished for association with Yang Ping and sent out as prefect of Kai.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was punished for his association with Yang Ping and sent out as prefect of Kai.

sentences.zh: 未幾卒。

translations.literal: Before long he died.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he died.

sentences.zh: 員工文辭，尚節義。

translations.literal: Yuan was skilled in literary composition and valued moral integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan was skilled in letters and prized moral integrity.

sentences.zh: 杜亞為東都留守，辟為從事、檢校員外郎。

translations.literal: Du Ya was eastern capital protector; he recruited [Yuan] as aide and acting vice director.
translations.idiomatic: When Du Ya was protector of the Eastern Capital, he recruited Yuan as aide and acting vice director.

sentences.zh: 早卒，有文集十卷。

translations.literal: He died early and left a collection of writings in ten chapters.
translations.idiomatic: He died young and left a collection of writings in ten chapters.

sentences.zh: 質兄弟俱有令譽而和粹，世以「滋味」目之：贊俗而有格，為酪；

translations.literal: The Zhi brothers all had fine reputations and were gentle and pure; the world called them by "flavors": Zan was common yet had style, like cheese;
translations.idiomatic: The Zhi brothers all enjoyed fine reputations and were gentle and pure; contemporaries likened them to "flavors": Zan was plain yet had character, like cheese;

sentences.zh: 質美而多入，為酥；

translations.literal: Zhi was fine and deeply appealing, like butter;
translations.idiomatic: Zhi was refined and deeply appealing, like butter;

sentences.zh: 員為醍醐；

translations.literal: Yuan was ghee;
translations.idiomatic: Yuan was clarified butter;

sentences.zh: 賞為乳腐。

translations.literal: Shang was fermented milk curd.
translations.idiomatic: Shang was fermented bean curd.

sentences.zh: 近代士大夫言家法者，以穆氏為高。

translations.literal: Among recent scholar-officials who spoke of family discipline, the Mu clan was held highest.
translations.idiomatic: Among recent scholar-officials who spoke of household discipline, the Mu clan was held in highest esteem.

sentences.zh: 崔邠，字處仁，清河武城人。

translations.literal: Cui Bin, courtesy name Churen, was a native of Wucheng in Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Bin, whose courtesy name was Churen, was from Wucheng in Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 祖結，父倕，官卑。

translations.literal: His grandfather was Jie; his father Zhi held low office.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather was Jie and his father Zhi held low office.

sentences.zh: 邠少舉進士，又登賢良方正科。

translations.literal: Bin in his youth passed the jinshi examination and also passed the Exemplary and Upright examination.
translations.idiomatic: Bin passed the jinshi examination in his youth and also passed the Exemplary and Upright examination.

sentences.zh: 貞元中授渭南尉。

translations.literal: In the Zhenyuan era he was appointed Wei of Weinan.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenyuan era he was appointed defender of Weinan.

sentences.zh: 遷拾遺、補闕。

translations.literal: He was promoted to remonstrator and then remonstrator of the left.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to remonstrator and then remonstrator of the left.

sentences.zh: 常疏論裴延齡，為時所知。

translations.literal: He often memorialized in criticism of Pei Yanling and was known to his age.
translations.idiomatic: He often memorialized against Pei Yanling and won recognition in his day.

sentences.zh: 以兵部員外郎知制誥至中書舍人，凡七年。

translations.literal: From vice director of the Ministry of War drafting edicts to Secretariat drafter, altogether seven years.
translations.idiomatic: From vice director of the Ministry of War drafting edicts to Secretariat drafter, he served seven years in all.

sentences.zh: 又權知吏部選事。

translations.literal: He also acted as overseer of Ministry of Personnel selections.
translations.idiomatic: He also served as acting overseer of Ministry of Personnel selections.

sentences.zh: 明年，為禮部侍郎，轉吏部侍郎，賜以金紫。

translations.literal: The next year he became vice minister of rites, then vice minister of personnel, and was granted the gold-purple insignia.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he became vice minister of rites, then vice minister of personnel, and was granted the gold-and-purple insignia.

sentences.zh: 邠溫裕沈密，尤敦清儉。

translations.literal: Bin was warm, generous, deep, and reserved, and especially devoted to purity and frugality.
translations.idiomatic: Bin was warm, reserved, and deeply principled, and especially devoted to purity and frugality.

sentences.zh: 上亦器重之。

translations.literal: The emperor also valued him highly.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also held him in high regard.

sentences.zh: 裴垍將引為相，病難於承答，事竟寢。

translations.literal: Pei Ji was about to bring him in as chief minister, but [Bin] fell ill and found it hard to respond; the matter was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Ji was about to bring him in as chief minister, but Bin fell ill and could not take on the role; the appointment was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 兄弟同時奉朝請者四人，頗以孝敬怡睦聞。

translations.literal: Four brothers at the same time attended court audiences; they were widely known for filial devotion and harmonious kinship.
translations.idiomatic: Four brothers served at court at the same time and were widely known for filial devotion and harmonious kinship.

sentences.zh: 後改太常卿，知吏部尚書銓事。

translations.literal: Later he was changed to director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and oversaw the Ministry of Personnel chief minister's selection affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was made director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and oversaw the chief minister of personnel's selection duties.

sentences.zh: 故事，太常卿初上，大閱《四部樂》於署，觀者縱焉。

translations.literal: By precedent, when a new director of sacrifices first took office, the Four Departments of Music were reviewed in full at the office, and spectators were unrestrained.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent, when a new director of sacrifices first took office, the Four Departments of Music were reviewed in full at the office, and the crowd was allowed to run freely.

sentences.zh: 邠自私第去帽，親導母輿，公卿逢者回騎避之，衢路以為榮。

translations.literal: Bin removed his cap at his private residence, personally guided his mother's carriage, and when high officials met him they turned their mounts aside; the streets regarded it as an honor.
translations.idiomatic: Bin removed his cap at his private residence and personally guided his mother's carriage; when high officials met him they turned their mounts aside, and the streets took it as an honor to witness.

sentences.zh: 居母憂，歲余卒，元和十年三月也，時年六十二。

translations.literal: While in mourning for his mother, he died a little over a year later, in the third month of the tenth year of Yuanhe, aged sixty-two.
translations.idiomatic: While in mourning for his mother he died a little over a year later, in the third month of the tenth year of Yuanhe, at the age of sixty-two.

sentences.zh: 贈吏部尚書，謚曰文簡。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made chief minister of personnel with the posthumous title Wénjiǎn.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made chief minister of personnel with the posthumous title Literary and Simple.

sentences.zh: 弟鄯、郾、鄲等六人。

translations.literal: His younger brothers Shan, Yan, and Tan—six men in all.
translations.idiomatic: He had six younger brothers, among them Shan, Yan, and Tan.

sentences.zh: 子璀、璜，璀子彥融，皆登進士第，歷位臺閣。

translations.literal: His sons Cui and Huang; Cui's son Yanrong—all passed the jinshi examination and served in posts at court.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Cui and Huang, and Cui's son Yanrong, all passed the jinshi examination and rose through posts at court.

sentences.zh: 鄯少有文學，舉進士。

translations.literal: Shan had literary talent from youth and passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: Shan showed literary promise from youth and passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 元和中，歷監察御史。

translations.literal: During the Yuanhe era he served as Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yuanhe era he served as investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 太和元年十月，自太子詹事拜左金吾衛大將軍。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the first year of Tahe, he was promoted from Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent to General of the Left Golden Crown Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of Tahe 1 he was promoted from grand mentor of the heir apparent to general of the Left Golden Crown Guard.

sentences.zh: 鄯昆弟六人，仕官皆至三品。

translations.literal: Shan's six brothers all reached third rank in office.
translations.idiomatic: All six of Shan's brothers rose to third rank.

sentences.zh: 邠、郾、鄲三人，知貢舉，掌銓衡。

translations.literal: Bin, Yan, and Tan—the three of them directed the imperial examinations and managed personnel selections.
translations.idiomatic: Bin, Yan, and Tan all directed the imperial examinations and oversaw personnel appointments.

sentences.zh: 冠族聞望，為時名德。

translations.literal: A foremost clan in reputation and prestige, they were celebrated men of virtue in their age.
translations.idiomatic: A leading clan in prestige and renown, they were celebrated as men of virtue in their time.

sentences.zh: 鄯太和九年冬，為左金吾大將軍，無病暴亡。

translations.literal: In winter of the ninth year of Taihe, Shan was left metropolitan commandant of the Majestic Guard and died suddenly without illness.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the ninth year of Taihe, Shan was serving as left metropolitan commandant of the Majestic Guard when he died suddenly without prior illness.

sentences.zh: 不旬日有訓、註之亂，其亂始自金吾。

translations.literal: Within ten days there was the rebellion of Xun and Zhu; the rebellion began from the Majestic Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Within ten days the Xun-Zhu Rebellion broke out, and it had its origin in the Majestic Guard.

sentences.zh: 君子乃知鄯之亡，崔氏積善之征也。

translations.literal: Men of principle then knew Shan's death was a sign of the Cui clan's accumulated virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Men of principle then understood that Shan's death was an omen of the Cui family's accumulated virtue.

sentences.zh: 贈禮部尚書。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made chief minister of rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made chief minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 子瑄。

translations.literal: His son was Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Xuan.

sentences.zh: 郾，字廣略。

translations.literal: Yan, courtesy name Guanglue.
translations.idiomatic: Yan, whose courtesy name was Guanglue.

sentences.zh: 舉進士，平判入等，授集賢殿校書郎。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination, entered grade through impartial evaluation, and was appointed collator of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination, qualified through the impartial evaluation, and was appointed collator at the Hall of Assembled Worthies.

sentences.zh: 三命升朝，為監察御史、刑部員外郎。

translations.literal: Three appointments brought him to court; he became investigating censor and vice director of the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: After three appointments he entered court service as investigating censor and vice director of the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 資質秀偉，神情重雅，人望而愛之，終不可舍，不知者以為事高簡，拘靜默耳。

translations.literal: His endowment was fine and imposing, his bearing grave and refined; people who saw him loved him and could not bear to part with him. Those who did not know him thought he merely affected lofty reserve and constrained silence.
translations.idiomatic: Fine-featured and imposing, grave and refined in bearing, he drew people's love at first sight and they found it hard to leave his company. Those who did not know him well assumed he merely affected lofty reserve and rigid silence.

sentences.zh: 居內憂，釋服為吏部員外。

translations.literal: While in inner mourning, after ending mourning garb he became vice director of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: While mourning for his father, upon ending the mourning period he became vice director of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 奸吏不敢欺，孤寒無援者未嘗留滯，銓敘之美，為時所稱。

translations.literal: Corrupt clerks did not dare to deceive him; the isolated and poor with no backing were never detained; the excellence of his selections was praised by the age.
translations.idiomatic: Corrupt clerks did not dare deceive him, and candidates who were isolated and without patrons were never left in limbo. The fairness of his personnel selections won praise in his day.

sentences.zh: 再遷左司郎中。

translations.literal: He was again promoted to left bureau director.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted again to director of the left bureau.

sentences.zh: 元和十三年，鄭余慶為禮儀詳定使，選時有禮學者共事，以郾為詳定判官、吏部郎中。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Yuanhe, Zheng Yuqing was commissioner for detailed determination of ritual, selecting men learned in ritual of the time to work with him; Yan was made determining judge and director of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of Yuanhe, Zheng Yuqing served as commissioner for the detailed determination of ritual and chose contemporary scholars of ritual to assist him; Yan was appointed determining judge and director of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 十五年，遷諫議大夫。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he was moved to grand remonstrator.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he was promoted to grand remonstrator.

sentences.zh: 穆宗即位，荒於禽酒，坐朝常晚。

translations.literal: When Muzong took the throne, he was wild with hunting and wine; sitting court was often late.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Muzong came to the throne, he abandoned himself to hunting and wine, and often held court late.

sentences.zh: 郾與同列鄭覃等延英切諫。

translations.literal: Yan and his colleagues Zheng Tan and others remonstrated sharply at the Yenying Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Yan and his colleagues Zheng Tan and others offered pointed remonstrance at the Yenying Audience Hall.

sentences.zh: 穆宗甚嘉之，畋遊稍簡。

translations.literal: Muzong greatly praised this; hunting excursions became somewhat reduced.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Muzong greatly approved, and his hunting excursions became somewhat less frequent.

sentences.zh: 長慶中，轉給事中。

translations.literal: In the Changqing era he was transferred to supervising secretary.
translations.idiomatic: During the Changqing era he was transferred to supervising secretary.

sentences.zh: 昭湣即位，選侍講學士，轉中書舍人。

translations.literal: When Zhaomin took the throne, he was selected as lecturer-in-attendance, then transferred to Secretariat drafter.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhaomin came to the throne, Yan was selected as lecturer-in-attendance and then promoted to Secretariat drafter.

sentences.zh: 入思政殿謝恩，奏曰：「陛下用臣為侍講，半歲有余，未嘗問臣經義。

translations.literal: Entering the Hall of Contemplating Governance to thank for grace, he memorialized, "Your Majesty employed your servant as lecturer-in-attendance for more than half a year, yet never asked your servant about the meaning of the classics.
translations.idiomatic: When he entered the Hall of Contemplating Governance to offer thanks, he said, "Your Majesty appointed me lecturer-in-attendance more than half a year ago, yet You have never asked me about the meaning of the classics.

sentences.zh: 今蒙轉改，實慚屍素，有愧厚恩。」

translations.literal: Now receiving transfer and promotion, I truly feel ashamed of occupying salary without merit and am unworthy of your thick grace."
translations.idiomatic: Now that I have been transferred and promoted, I am ashamed of drawing salary without earning it and feel unworthy of Your gracious favor."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「朕機務稍閑，即當請益。」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "When my pressing affairs are somewhat free, I shall at once seek increase in learning."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "When my state duties allow a little leisure, I shall ask you to instruct me."

sentences.zh: 高鉞曰：「陛下意雖樂善，既未延接儒生，天下之人，寧知重道？」

translations.literal: Gao Xian said, "Your Majesty's intent though loves the good, since you have not yet extended audience to Confucian scholars, the people of the empire—how would they know to honor the Way?"
translations.idiomatic: Gao Xian said, "Your Majesty's heart may delight in goodness, but since You have not yet received Confucian scholars in audience, how can the people under heaven know that You honor the Way?"

sentences.zh: 帝深引咎，賜之錦彩。

translations.literal: The emperor deeply blamed himself and bestowed brocades and colors on them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took the criticism deeply to heart and rewarded them with brocades and silks.

sentences.zh: 郾退，與同列高重抄撮《六經》嘉言要道，區分事類，凡十卷，名曰《諸經纂要》，冀人主易於省覽。

translations.literal: Yan withdrew and, with his colleague Gao Chong, excerpted fine words and essential doctrines from the Six Classics, divided them by category into ten chapters in all entitled Essentials Drawn from the Classics, hoping the ruler would find them easy to review.
translations.idiomatic: After withdrawing, Yan and his colleague Gao Chong excerpted fine passages and essential doctrines from the Six Classics, arranged them by topic into ten chapters entitled Essentials Drawn from the Classics, hoping the sovereign would find them easy to review at a glance.

sentences.zh: 上嘉之，賜錦彩二百匹、銀器等。

translations.literal: The emperor praised it and granted two hundred bolts of brocade and silks, silver vessels, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved and granted two hundred bolts of brocades and silks, silver vessels, and the like.

sentences.zh: 其年轉禮部侍郎，東都試舉人。

translations.literal: That year he was transferred to vice minister of rites and tested candidates at the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: That year he was made vice minister of rites and conducted the examination of candidates at the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 凡兩歲掌貢士，平心閱試，賞拔藝能，所擢者無非名士，至大中、咸通之代，為輔相名卿者十數人。

translations.literal: For two years in charge of presenting scholars, he examined with even heart, rewarded and elevated talent and ability; those he promoted were none but famous scholars, and by the Dazhong and Xiantong eras more than ten became chief ministers and eminent ministers.
translations.idiomatic: For two years he oversaw the presentation of candidates, examining them impartially and promoting talent; every man he advanced became a noted scholar, and by the Dazhong and Xiantong periods more than ten of them had risen to chief ministerships and other eminent posts.

sentences.zh: 出為陜州觀察使。

translations.literal: He went out as governor of Shaanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as governor of Shaanzhou.

sentences.zh: 舊弊有上供不足，奪吏俸以益之，歲八十萬，郾以廉使常用之直代之。

translations.literal: An old abuse was that when tribute to the capital fell short, officials' salaries were seized to make up the sum—eighty thousand per year; Yan replaced it with the regular market price used by the fiscal commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: An old abuse held that when local tribute to the capital fell short, officials' salaries were seized to make up the deficit—eighty thousand strings per year. Yan substituted the standard market price used by the fiscal inspector.

sentences.zh: 居二年，政績聞於朝。

translations.literal: After two years, his administrative achievements were heard of at court.
translations.idiomatic: After two years his administrative accomplishments were known at court.

sentences.zh: 遷鄂嶽安黃等州觀察使。

translations.literal: He was moved to regional inspector of E, Yue, An, Huang, and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to regional inspector of E, Yue, An, Huang, and other prefectures.

sentences.zh: 又五年，移浙西道都團練觀察使，至，用寬政安疲人。

translations.literal: After five more years he was transferred to overall military governor and regional inspector of Zhexi Circuit; upon arrival he used lenient governance to settle the weary people.
translations.idiomatic: Five years later he was transferred to overall military governor and regional inspector of Zhexi Circuit, where he governed leniently to bring relief to the exhausted populace.

sentences.zh: 及居鄂渚，則峻法嚴刑，未常貰一死罪。

translations.literal: When he resided at the E region, then strict law and severe punishments; he never once pardoned a capital offense.
translations.idiomatic: During his tenure at Ezhou he applied stern law and severe punishments and never once commuted a capital sentence.

sentences.zh: 江湖之間，萑蒲是叢，因造蒙沖小艦，上下千里，期月而盡獲群盜。

translations.literal: Between river and lake thickets of reeds were crowded; he therefore built covered assault boats, up and down a thousand li, and within a month captured all bandit bands.
translations.idiomatic: Between the rivers and lakes bandits flourished in dense thickets; he built light covered assault vessels and, patrolling a thousand li within a month, captured every bandit band.

sentences.zh: 凡三按廉車，率由清簡少事，財用有余，遂寧泰。

translations.literal: Altogether three times he inspected as fiscal commissioner; in each case through purity and simplicity with few affairs, finances had surplus, and peace and security followed.
translations.idiomatic: Over three terms as regional inspector he governed with integrity and restraint, keeping administration lean; surplus funds accumulated and the regions grew secure and tranquil.

sentences.zh: 開成元年卒，年六十九，贈吏部尚書，謚曰德。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kaicheng he died, aged sixty-nine; posthumously made chief minister of personnel, posthumous title Dé.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the first year of Kaicheng at the age of sixty-nine. He was posthumously made chief minister of personnel with the posthumous title Virtuous.

sentences.zh: 郾與兄邠、弟鄲等皆有令譽。

translations.literal: Yan, with elder brother Bin and younger brother Tan and the rest, all had fine reputations.
translations.idiomatic: Yan, his elder brother Bin, his younger brother Tan, and the others all enjoyed fine reputations.

sentences.zh: 而郾疏財恢廓，昆仲所不及。

translations.literal: But Yan was liberal with wealth and broad-minded, which his brothers could not match.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Yan surpassed his brothers in generosity and magnanimity.

sentences.zh: 子瑤、瑰、瑾、珮、璆。

translations.literal: His sons were Yao, Gui, Jin, Pei, and Qiu.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Yao, Gui, Jin, Pei, and Qiu.

sentences.zh: 瑤，太和三年登進士第，出佐籓方，入升朝列，累至中書舍人。

translations.literal: Yao, in the third year of Taihe passed jinshi, went out to assist a frontier province, entered and rose in court ranks, accumulating to Secretariat drafter.
translations.idiomatic: Yao passed the jinshi examination in the third year of Taihe, served as aide in a frontier province, then entered central office and rose to Secretariat drafter.

sentences.zh: 大中六年，知貢舉，旋拜禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Dazhong he oversaw presenting scholars, and soon was made vice minister of rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Dazhong he oversaw the imperial examination and was soon appointed vice minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 出為浙西觀察使，又遷鄂州刺史、鄂嶽觀察使，終於位。

translations.literal: He went out as regional inspector of Zhexi, then was moved to prefect of Ezhou and regional inspector of E and Yue, dying in office.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as regional inspector of Zhexi, then transferred to prefect of Ezhou and regional inspector of E and Yue, where he died in office.

sentences.zh: 瑰、珮、璆官至郎署給諫。

translations.literal: Gui, Pei, and Qiu reached offices in secretariat bureaus, supervising secretaries and remonstrators.
translations.idiomatic: Gui, Pei, and Qiu rose to posts in the Secretariat bureaus as supervising secretaries and remonstrators.

sentences.zh: 謹，大中十年登進士第，累居使府，歷尚書郎、知制誥。

translations.literal: Jin, in the tenth year of Dazhong passed jinshi, repeatedly served in commissioner staffs, and passed through director of a ministry and drafter of edicts.
translations.idiomatic: Jin passed the jinshi examination in the tenth year of Dazhong, served repeatedly on commissioner staffs, and rose through posts as director in a ministry and drafter of edicts.

sentences.zh: 咸通十三年，知貢舉，選拔頗為得人。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Xiantong he oversaw presenting scholars; selections were quite successful in getting the right men.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of Xiantong he oversaw the examination and selected candidates with notable success.

sentences.zh: 尋拜禮部侍郎，出為湖南觀察使。

translations.literal: Soon he was made vice minister of rites and went out as regional inspector of Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed vice minister of rites and sent out as regional inspector of Hunan.

sentences.zh: 鄲，登進士第，累遷監察御史，三遷考功郎中。

translations.literal: Tan passed jinshi, was repeatedly promoted to investigating censor, and three times promoted to director of merit evaluation.
translations.idiomatic: Tan passed the jinshi examination, rose through posts to investigating censor, and after three promotions became director of the Office of Merit Evaluation.

sentences.zh: 太和三年，以本官充翰林學士，轉中書舍人。

translations.literal: In the third year of Taihe, with his existing office he filled Hanlin academician, then transferred to Secretariat drafter.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Taihe he was appointed Hanlin academician while retaining his current rank, then promoted to Secretariat drafter.

sentences.zh: 六年，罷學士。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, dismissed as academician.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was dismissed from the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 八年，為工部侍郎、集賢殿學士，權知禮部，真拜兵部侍郎，本官判吏部東銓事。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was vice minister of works and academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, acting head of the Ministry of Rites, truly appointed vice minister of war, and in his existing office adjudicated eastern selections of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he became vice minister of works and academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, served as acting head of the Ministry of Rites, was formally appointed vice minister of war, and while retaining that rank oversaw the eastern selection board of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 文宗勤於政道，每苦選曹訛弊，延英謂宰臣曰：「吏部殊不選才，安得摭實無濫，可厘革否？」

translations.literal: Wenzong was diligent in the way of governance, often vexed by abuses in the selection bureau; at Yenying he told chief ministers, "The Ministry of Personnel utterly fails to select talent—how can we gather reality without overflow? Can it be reformed?"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wenzong was diligent in governance and often troubled by abuses in the selection office. At the Yenying Audience he told his chief ministers, "The Ministry of Personnel hardly selects for talent at all. How can we appoint men on merit without padding the rolls? Can this be reformed?"

sentences.zh: 李石對曰：「令錄可以商量，他官且宜循舊。」

translations.literal: Li Shi replied, "District magistrates and recorders can be discussed; other offices should for now follow the old."
translations.idiomatic: Li Shi replied, "We might reconsider appointments for district magistrates and recorders, but other offices should continue under the old rules for now."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「循舊如配官耳，賢不肖安能甄別？」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Following the old is like assigning offices by quota—how can worth and unworth be distinguished?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Following the old way is no better than filling quotas—how can we tell the worthy from the unworthy?"

sentences.zh: 帝召三銓謂之曰：「卿等比選令錄，如何註擬？」

translations.literal: The emperor summoned the three selection directors and said, "You lately select magistrates and recorders—how do you register and propose?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned the three directors of selection and asked, "When you appoint district magistrates and recorders, what criteria do you use?"

sentences.zh: 鄲對曰：「資敘相當，問其為治之術，視可否而擬之。」

translations.literal: Tan replied, "When qualifications and seniority match, ask their methods of governance and, viewing whether feasible, propose accordingly."
translations.idiomatic: Tan replied, "When their qualifications and seniority are appropriate, we ask about their methods of governance and propose appointments according to what seems feasible."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「依資合得，而才劣者何授？」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "By seniority they qualify, but what is given those inferior in talent?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked, "If they qualify by seniority but lack ability, what posts do they receive?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「與邊遠慢官。」

translations.literal: He replied, "Give them remote border posts of little consequence."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "We assign them to remote border posts of little importance."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「如以不肖之才治邊民，則疾苦可知也。

translations.literal: The emperor said, "If unworthy talent governs border people, their suffering is knowable.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "If unworthy men govern border peoples, their suffering is easy to imagine.

sentences.zh: 凡朝廷求理，遠近皆須得人。

translations.literal: Wherever the court seeks good order, near and far all must get the right men.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever the court seeks good governance, near and far alike require able men.

sentences.zh: 茍非其才，人受其弊矣。」

translations.literal: If it is not the right talent, the people suffer the harm."
translations.idiomatic: If the wrong men are appointed, the people bear the harm."

sentences.zh: 尋拜吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: Soon he was made vice minister of personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after, Tan was appointed vice minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 開成二年，出為宣州刺史，兼御史中丞、宣歙觀察使。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kaicheng he went out as prefect of Xuanzhou, concurrently censor-in-chief and regional inspector of Xuan and She.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Kaicheng he was sent out as prefect of Xuanzhou, concurrently censor-in-chief and regional inspector of Xuan and She.

sentences.zh: 四年，入為太常卿。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he entered as director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he returned to court as director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 七月，以本官同中書門下平章事，尋加中書侍郎、銀青光祿大夫。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, with his existing office he became associate commissioner of the Chancellery and Secretariat, soon added vice director of the Secretariat and grand master with silver-blue seal and purple robes.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month he was made chief minister while retaining his current rank, and was soon also appointed vice director of the Secretariat and grand master with silver-blue seal and purple robes.

sentences.zh: 會昌初，李德裕用事，與鄲弟兄素善。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Huichang, Li Deyu held power; he and Tan's brothers were old friends.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Huichang era Li Deyu held power, and he had long been on good terms with Tan and his brothers.

sentences.zh: 鄲在相位累年，歷方鎮、太子師保卒。

translations.literal: Tan was in the chief-ministerial position for accumulated years, passed through regional commands and tutor-protector of the heir apparent, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Tan served as chief minister for many years, later held regional commands and posts as tutor and protector of the heir apparent, and died in office.

sentences.zh: 竇群，字丹列，扶風平陵人。

translations.literal: Dou Qun, courtesy name Danlie, was a native of Pingling in Fufeng.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Qun, whose courtesy name was Danlie, was from Pingling in Fufeng.

sentences.zh: 祖亶，同昌郡司馬。

translations.literal: His grandfather was Dan, military aide of Tongchang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Dan served as military aide of Tongchang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父叔向，以工詩稱，代宗朝，官至左拾遺。

translations.literal: His father Shuxiang was famed for skill in poetry; in the Daizong reign he reached left remonstrator.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shuxiang was renowned for his poetry and rose during Emperor Daizong's reign to left remonstrator.

sentences.zh: 群兄常、牟，弟鞏，皆登進士第，唯群獨為處士，隱居毗陵，以節操聞。

translations.literal: Qun's elder brothers Chang and Mou and younger brother Gong all passed jinshi; Qun alone was a retired scholar, living in seclusion at Piling, known for moral integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Qun's elder brothers Chang and Mou and his younger brother Gong all passed the jinshi examination; Qun alone remained a retired scholar, living in seclusion at Piling, where he was known for his integrity.

sentences.zh: 及母卒，嚙一指置棺中，因廬墓次終喪。

translations.literal: When his mother died, he bit off a finger and placed it in the coffin, then built a hut beside the grave and completed mourning.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died, he bit off one finger and placed it in her coffin, then lived in a hut beside her grave until the mourning period was complete.

sentences.zh: 後學《春秋》於啖助之門人盧庇者，著書三十四卷，號《史記名臣疏》。

translations.literal: Later he studied the Spring and Autumn Annals under Lu Pi, a disciple of Tan Zhu, and composed a work in thirty-four scrolls entitled Commentary on Famous Ministers in the Records of the Grand Historian.
translations.idiomatic: He later studied the Spring and Autumn Annals under Lu Pi, a disciple of Tan Zhu, and wrote a thirty-four-scroll work called Commentary on Famous Ministers in the Records of the Grand Historian.

sentences.zh: 貞元中，蘇州刺史韋夏卿以丘園茂異薦，兼獻其書，不報。

translations.literal: During the Zhenyuan era, Wei Xiaqing, Prefect of Suzhou, recommended him as an eminent recluse of hill and garden, and also presented his book, but there was no response.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhenyuan era, Wei Xiaqing, prefect of Suzhou, recommended him as a distinguished recluse and submitted his book to the throne, but received no reply.

sentences.zh: 及夏卿入為吏部侍郎，改京兆尹，中謝日，因對復薦群。

translations.literal: When Xiaqing entered the capital as Vice Minister of the Ministry of Personnel and was transferred to be Metropolitan Magistrate of Jingzhao, on the day of his mid-audience thanksgiving he took the opportunity while in audience to recommend Qun again.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaqing entered the capital as vice minister of personnel and was reassigned as metropolitan magistrate of Jingzhao, he used his mid-audience to recommend Qun once more.

sentences.zh: 征拜左拾遺，遷侍御史，充入蕃使秘書監張薦判官。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed Left Reminder, then promoted to Assistant Censor, and served as aide to Zhang Jian, Director of the Secretariat, on an embassy to the foreign states.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned and appointed left reminder, then promoted to assistant censor and made aide to Zhang Jian, director of the secretariat, on an embassy to the border peoples.

sentences.zh: 群因入對，奏曰：「陛下即位二十年，始自草澤擢臣為拾遺，是難其進也。

translations.literal: Qun took the occasion of an audience to memorialize, saying: "Your Majesty has reigned for twenty years before raising me from the grasslands and marshes to the post of Reminder—thus making my advancement difficult.
translations.idiomatic: When Qun had an audience, he memorialized: "Your Majesty has reigned twenty years before plucking me from obscurity to make me a reminder—that was making advancement hard for me.

sentences.zh: 今陛下以二十年難進之臣，用為和蕃判官，一何易也？」

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty uses a minister whose advancement was difficult for twenty years as an aide on a peace mission to the foreign tribes—how easy this is!"
translations.idiomatic: Now Your Majesty appoints a man it took twenty years to promote as an aide on a peace mission to the tribes—how easy that is!"

sentences.zh: 德宗異其言，留之，復為侍御史。

translations.literal: Emperor Dezong was struck by his words, kept him at court, and restored him to the post of Assistant Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Dezong was impressed by his words, kept him at court, and restored him to assistant censor.

sentences.zh: 王叔文之黨柳宗元、劉禹錫皆慢群，群不附之。

translations.literal: Wang Shuwen's faction—Liu Zongyuan and Liu Yuxi—both treated Qun with disdain, and Qun would not join them.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zongyuan and Liu Yuxi, members of Wang Shuwen's faction, both looked down on Qun, and Qun would not align with them.

sentences.zh: 其黨議欲貶群官，韋執誼止之。

translations.literal: His faction deliberated demoting Qun, but Wei Zhiyi stopped them.
translations.idiomatic: The faction considered demoting Qun, but Wei Zhiyi prevented it.

sentences.zh: 群嘗謁王叔文，叔文命撤榻而進。

translations.literal: Qun once paid a call on Wang Shuwen; Shuwen ordered his couch removed and then received him.
translations.idiomatic: Qun once visited Wang Shuwen, who had his couch taken away before admitting him.

sentences.zh: 群揖之曰：「夫事有不可知者。」

translations.literal: Qun bowed to him and said: "There are things in affairs that cannot be foreknown."
translations.idiomatic: Qun bowed and said: "Some things in life cannot be foreseen."

sentences.zh: 叔文曰：「如何？」

translations.literal: Shuwen said: "Such as what?"
translations.idiomatic: Shuwen asked: "Such as what?"

sentences.zh: 群曰：「去年李實伐恩恃貴，傾動一時，此時公逡巡路旁，乃江南一吏耳。

translations.literal: Qun said: "Last year Li Shi relied on favor and noble rank to boast of his merit and shook the age; at that time you loitered by the roadside—you were merely a petty official from Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Qun said: "Last year Li Shi traded on imperial favor and high rank, swaggering through the court; then you waited in the wings—you were only a minor official from the south.

sentences.zh: 今公已處實形勢，又安得不慮路旁有公者乎？」

translations.literal: Now that you hold a position of real power, how can you fail to consider that there may be someone like you loitering by the roadside?"
translations.idiomatic: Now that you hold real power, how can you not wonder whether someone like you is waiting in the wings?"

sentences.zh: 叔文雖異其言，竟不之用。

translations.literal: Although Shuwen was struck by his words, in the end he did not employ him.
translations.idiomatic: Shuwen was struck by the warning, but in the end he never made use of Qun.

sentences.zh: 憲宗即位，轉膳部員外，兼侍御史知雜，出為唐州刺史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xianzong took the throne, Qun was transferred to External Affairs Secretary of the Ministry of Rites, concurrently serving as Assistant Censor in charge of miscellaneous duties, and was sent out as Prefect of Tangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xianzong ascended the throne, Qun was made external affairs secretary in the ministry of rites and assistant censor in charge of miscellaneous cases, then sent out as prefect of Tangzhou.

sentences.zh: 節度使於頔素聞其名，既謁見，群危言激切，頔甚悅。

translations.literal: Military Commissioner Yu Di had long heard of his reputation; after Qun paid his respects, Qun spoke in stern and passionate terms, and Di was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Military Commissioner Yu Di had long known Qun's reputation; when Qun presented himself, Qun spoke bluntly and forcefully, and Di was greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 奏留充山南東道節度副使、檢校兵部郎中，兼御史中丞，賜紫金魚袋。

translations.literal: He memorialized to retain Qun as Vice Military Commissioner of the Shan'nan East Circuit, Checked Rank Director of the Ministry of War, concurrently Vice Censor-in-Chief, and bestowed a purple robe and gold fish tally.
translations.idiomatic: Di memorialized to keep Qun as vice commissioner of the Shan'nan East circuit, checked-rank director in the ministry of war and vice censor-in-chief, and granted him the purple robe and gold fish tally.

sentences.zh: 宰相武元衡、李吉甫皆愛重之，召入為吏部郎中。

translations.literal: Chief Ministers Wu Yuanheng and Li Jifu both cherished and valued him, and he was recalled to serve as Director of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Chief ministers Wu Yuanheng and Li Jifu both admired him, and he was recalled to serve as director of the ministry of personnel.

sentences.zh: 元衡輔政，舉群代己為中丞。

translations.literal: When Yuanheng assisted in government, he recommended Qun to succeed himself as Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: While Yuanheng was chief minister, he recommended Qun to succeed him as censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 群奏刑部郎中呂溫、羊士諤為御史。

translations.literal: Qun memorialized that Lü Wen and Yang Shi'e, Directors of the Ministry of Justice, be appointed censors.
translations.idiomatic: Qun recommended Lü Wen and Yang Shi'e, directors in the ministry of justice, for appointment as censors.

sentences.zh: 吉甫以羊、呂險躁，持之數日不下，群等怒怨吉甫。

translations.literal: Jifu regarded Yang and Lü as rash and reckless; he held the memorial for several days without approving it, and Qun and the others resented Jifu in anger.
translations.idiomatic: Jifu considered Yang and Lü rash and impulsive, held the nominations for days without acting, and Qun and his allies grew angry at Jifu.

sentences.zh: 三年八月，吉甫罷相，出鎮淮南，群等欲因失恩傾之。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the third year, Jifu was dismissed as chief minister and sent out to command Huainan; Qun and the others wished to take advantage of his loss of favor to overthrow him.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the third year Jifu was removed as chief minister and posted to Huainan; Qun and his allies hoped to use his fall from favor to bring him down.

sentences.zh: 吉甫嘗召術士陳登宿於安邑裏第。

translations.literal: Jifu had once summoned the magician Chen Deng to lodge at his residence in Anyi Lane.
translations.idiomatic: Jifu had once invited the diviner Chen Deng to stay at his house in Anyi Lane.

sentences.zh: 翌日，群令吏捕登考劾，偽構吉甫陰事，密以上聞。

translations.literal: The next day Qun ordered officials to arrest Deng for investigation, falsely fabricating secret misdeeds of Jifu and reporting them confidentially to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Qun had officials arrest Deng for interrogation, fabricating secret crimes against Jifu and reporting them privately to the throne.

sentences.zh: 帝召登面訊之，立辯其偽。

translations.literal: The emperor summoned Deng for face-to-face questioning; he immediately argued the charges were false.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned Deng and questioned him in person; Deng at once refuted the accusations as false.

sentences.zh: 憲宗怒，將誅群等，吉甫救之，出為湖南觀察使。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzong was enraged and was about to execute Qun and the others; Jifu saved them, and Qun was sent out as Military Commissioner of Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzong was furious and nearly had Qun and his allies executed; Jifu interceded for them, and Qun was sent out as military commissioner of Hunan.

sentences.zh: 數日，改黔州刺史、黔州觀察使。

translations.literal: Within several days he was transferred to be Prefect of Qianzhou and Military Commissioner of Qian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Within days he was reassigned as prefect of Qianzhou and military commissioner of Qian prefecture.

sentences.zh: 在黔中，屬大水壞其城郭，復築其城，征督溪洞諸蠻。

translations.literal: While in Qianzhong, a great flood damaged the city walls; he rebuilt the city and levied and supervised the various barbarian peoples of the stream valleys and cave settlements.
translations.idiomatic: While governing Qianzhong, a great flood destroyed the city walls; he rebuilt the city and pressed the stream-dwelling and cave-dwelling tribes for labor and tribute.

sentences.zh: 程作頗急，於是，辰、錦生蠻乘險作亂，群討之不能定。

translations.literal: The project was rushed; thereupon the raw barbarians of Chen and Jin took advantage of the terrain to rise in revolt, and Qun campaigned against them but could not pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: The work was hurried, and the unassimilated tribes of Chen and Jin seized the mountain passes to rebel; Qun attacked them but could not restore order.

sentences.zh: 六年九月，貶開州刺史。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the sixth year he was demoted to Prefect of Kaizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the sixth year he was demoted to prefect of Kaizhou.

sentences.zh: 在郡二年，改容州刺史、容管經略觀察使。

translations.literal: After two years in the prefecture he was transferred to be Prefect of Rongzhou and Military Commissioner and Commander-in-Chief of the Rong Administration Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: After two years in office he was transferred to prefect of Rongzhou and military commissioner of the Rong administration circuit.

sentences.zh: 九年，詔還朝，至衡州病卒，時年五十。

translations.literal: In the ninth year an edict recalled him to court; he died of illness at Hengzhou, aged fifty.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year an edict recalled him to court, but he died of illness at Hengzhou at the age of fifty.

sentences.zh: 群性狠戾，頗復恩讎，臨事不顧生死。

translations.literal: Qun was by nature fierce and perverse, given to repaying both kindness and vengeance, and in affairs he did not shrink from life or death.
translations.idiomatic: Qun was fierce and unforgiving by nature, quick to repay both favors and grudges, and in a crisis he cared nothing for his own life.

sentences.zh: 是時征入，雲欲大用，人皆懼駭，聞其卒方安。

translations.literal: At that time he was summoned to the capital, and it was said he would be greatly employed; everyone was fearful and alarmed, and only upon hearing of his death did they feel secure.
translations.idiomatic: When he was summoned to the capital, rumor held that he would be given great power; people were terrified, and only when news of his death arrived did they breathe easier.

sentences.zh: 二子：謙余、審余。

translations.literal: He had two sons: Qianyu and Shenyu.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons: Qianyu and Shenyu.

sentences.zh: 兄常，字中行，大歷十四年登進士第，居廣陵之柳楊。

translations.literal: His elder brother Chang, styled Zhongxing, passed the jinshi examination in the fourteenth year of the Dali era and lived at Liuyang in Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Chang, courtesy name Zhongxing, passed the jinshi examination in the fourteenth year of Dali and lived at Liuyang in Guangling.

sentences.zh: 結廬種樹，不求茍進，以講學著書為事，凡二十年不出。

translations.literal: He built a hut, planted trees, sought no careless advancement, and devoted himself to lecturing and writing books—for twenty years altogether he did not go out.
translations.idiomatic: He built a cottage, planted trees, refused to chase office by unworthy means, and spent twenty years teaching and writing without leaving home.

sentences.zh: 貞元十四年，鎮州節度使王武俊聞其賢，遣人致聘，辟為掌書記，不就。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Zhenyuan, Wang Wujun, military commissioner of Zhenzhou, heard of his worth and sent someone to extend an invitation, appointing him chief secretary—but he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year of Zhenyuan, Wang Wujun, military commissioner of Zhenzhou, heard of his learning and sent an envoy to invite him as chief secretary, but Chang declined.

sentences.zh: 其年，杜佑鎮淮南，奏授校書郎，為節度參謀。

translations.literal: That same year Du You commanded Huainan and memorialized to grant him the post of Proofreader, making him a strategic adviser to the military commission.
translations.idiomatic: That year Du You took command of Huainan, memorialized to appoint him proofreader, and made him a staff strategist.

sentences.zh: 元和六年，自湖南判官入為侍御史，轉水部員外郎。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Yuanhe he entered the capital from his post as aide in Hunan to serve as Assistant Censor, then was transferred to External Affairs Secretary of the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Yuanhe he came to court from his post as Hunan aide, became assistant censor, and was then promoted to external affairs secretary in the ministry of works.

sentences.zh: 出為朗州刺史，歷固陵、潯陽、臨川三郡守。

translations.literal: He was sent out as Prefect of Langzhou and successively served as prefect of the three prefectures of Guling, Xunyang, and Linchuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as prefect of Langzhou and later governed the three prefectures of Guling, Xunyang, and Linchuan in succession.

sentences.zh: 入為國子祭酒，求致仕。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as Chancellor of the Directorate of Education and requested retirement.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to the capital as chancellor of the directorate of education and asked to retire.

sentences.zh: 寶曆元年卒，時年七十。

translations.literal: He died in the first year of Baoli, aged seventy.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the first year of Baoli at the age of seventy.

sentences.zh: 子弘余，會昌中為黃州刺史。

translations.literal: His son Hongyu served as Prefect of Huangzhou during the Huichang era.
translations.idiomatic: His son Hongyu served as prefect of Huangzhou during the Huichang reign.

sentences.zh: 牟，字貽周。

translations.literal: Mou, styled Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Mou, courtesy name Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 貞元二年登進士第，試秘書省校書郎、東都留守巡官。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenyuan he passed the jinshi examination, was tested as Proofreader of the Secretariat, and served as circuit inspector for the Eastern Capital Garrison Commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhenyuan he passed the jinshi examination, served as a proofreader in the secretariat, and became an inspector for the eastern capital garrison.

sentences.zh: 歷河陽、昭義從事，檢校水部郎中，賜緋，再為留守判官。

translations.literal: He successively served as staff member under the Hedong and Zhaoyi commands, was Checked Rank Director of the Ministry of Works, was granted the crimson robe, and twice served as aide to the Garrison Commander.
translations.idiomatic: He served on the staffs of the Hedong and Zhaoyi commands, became checked-rank director in the ministry of works, received the crimson robe, and twice served as aide to the garrison commander.

sentences.zh: 入為都官郎中，出為澤州刺史，入為國子祭酒。
