translations.literal: He entered the capital as Director of the Ministry of Punishments, went out as Prefect of Zezhou, and returned to serve as Chancellor of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court as director of the ministry of punishments, went out as prefect of Zezhou, and returned as chancellor of the directorate of education.

sentences.zh: 長慶二年卒，時年七十四。

translations.literal: He died in the second year of Changqing, aged seventy-four.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the second year of Changqing at the age of seventy-four.

sentences.zh: 子周余，大中年秘書監。

translations.literal: His son Zhouyu served as Director of the Secretariat during the Dazhong era.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhouyu served as director of the secretariat during the Dazhong reign.

sentences.zh: 牟弟庠，字胃卿，釋褐國子主簿。

translations.literal: Mou's younger brother Ku, styled Weiqing, upon removing his commoner's garb was appointed Principal Clerk of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Mou's younger brother Ku, courtesy name Weiqing, entered office as principal clerk of the directorate of education.

sentences.zh: 吏部侍郎韓臯出鎮武昌，辟為推官。

translations.literal: Han Gao, Vice Minister of Personnel, went out to command Wuchang and appointed him as investigating officer.
translations.idiomatic: When Han Gao, vice minister of personnel, took command of Wuchang, he appointed Ku as investigating officer.

sentences.zh: 臯移鎮浙西，奏庠為節度副使、殿中侍御史，遷澤州刺史。

translations.literal: When Gao transferred to command Zhexi, he memorialized to make Ku Vice Military Commissioner and Palace Assistant Censor, and Ku was promoted to Prefect of Zezhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao moved to Zhexi, he memorialized to make Ku vice military commissioner and palace assistant censor; Ku was later promoted to prefect of Zezhou.

sentences.zh: 又為宣歙副使，除奉天令、登州刺史、東都留守判官，歷信、婺二州刺史。

translations.literal: He also served as deputy military commissioner of Xuanshe, was appointed Magistrate of Fengtian, Prefect of Dengzhou, aide to the Eastern Capital Garrison Commander, and successively Prefect of Xin and Wu prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: He also served as deputy commissioner of Xuanshe, then as magistrate of Fengtian, prefect of Dengzhou, aide to the eastern capital garrison, and in succession prefect of Xin and Wu.

sentences.zh: 卒年六十三。

translations.literal: He died at the age of sixty-three.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of sixty-three.

sentences.zh: 子繇、載。

translations.literal: His sons were You and Zai.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were You and Zai.

sentences.zh: 鞏，字友封，元和二年登進士第。

translations.literal: Gong, styled Youfeng, passed the jinshi examination in the second year of Yuanhe.
translations.idiomatic: Gong, courtesy name Youfeng, passed the jinshi examination in the second year of Yuanhe.

sentences.zh: 袁滋鎮滑州，辟為從事。

translations.literal: When Yuan Zi commanded Huazhou, he appointed Gong as a staff member.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Zi took command of Huazhou, he recruited Gong to his staff.

sentences.zh: 滋改荊、襄二鎮，皆從之，掌管記之任。

translations.literal: When Zi transferred to the two commands of Jing and Xiang, Gong followed him on both occasions and held the post of chief recorder.
translations.idiomatic: When Zi moved to the Jing and Xiang commands, Gong followed him each time and served as chief recorder.

sentences.zh: 平盧薛平又辟為副使。

translations.literal: Xue Ping of Pinglu also appointed him as deputy commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Ping of Pinglu also appointed him deputy commissioner.

sentences.zh: 入朝，拜侍御史，歷司勛員外、刑部郎中。

translations.literal: He entered the capital and was appointed Palace Censor, then successively served as External Affairs Secretary of the Ministry of Merit Awards and Director of the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court as palace censor, then served in succession as external affairs secretary in the ministry of merit awards and director in the ministry of justice.

sentences.zh: 元稹觀察浙東，奉為副使、檢校秘書少監，兼御史中丞，賜金紫。

translations.literal: When Yuan Zhen served as military commissioner of Zhedong, he appointed Gong deputy commissioner, Checked Rank Vice Director of the Secretariat, concurrently Vice Censor-in-Chief, and bestowed gold and purple.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Zhen governed Zhedong, he made Gong his deputy, checked-rank vice director of the secretariat and vice censor-in-chief, and granted him gold and purple insignia.

sentences.zh: 稹移鎮武昌，鞏又從之。

translations.literal: When Zhen transferred to command Wuchang, Gong followed him again.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhen moved to Wuchang, Gong followed him again.

sentences.zh: 鞏能五言詩，昆仲之間，與牟詩俱為時所賞重。

translations.literal: Gong was skilled at five-character poetry; among the brothers, his poems together with Mou's were both prized in their day.
translations.idiomatic: Gong wrote fine five-character verse; among the brothers, his poetry and Mou's were both highly regarded.

sentences.zh: 性溫雅，多不能持論，士友言議之際，吻動而不發，白居易等目為「囁嚅翁」。

translations.literal: He was gentle and refined by nature and often could not sustain an argument; when gentlemen and friends engaged in discussion his lips would move yet no words would come forth—Bai Juyi and others called him the "Muttering Old Man."
translations.idiomatic: Gentle and soft-spoken by nature, he rarely held his own in debate; at gatherings of friends his lips would move but no argument would emerge, and Bai Juyi and others nicknamed him the "Muttering Old Man."

sentences.zh: 終於鄂渚，時年六十。

translations.literal: He died at Ezhou, aged sixty.
translations.idiomatic: He died at Ezhou at the age of sixty.

sentences.zh: 子六人，景余、師裕最知名。

translations.literal: He had six sons; Jingyu and Shiyu were the most renowned.
translations.idiomatic: He had six sons; Jingyu and Shiyu were the best known.

sentences.zh: 李遜，字友道，後魏申公發之後，於趙郡謂之申公房。

translations.literal: Li Xun, styled Youdao, was a descendant of Duke Shen Fa of Northern Wei; in Zhao Prefecture they were called the House of Duke Shen.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xun, courtesy name Youdao, traced his descent to Duke Shen Fa of Northern Wei; in Zhao commandery the family was known as the House of Duke Shen.

sentences.zh: 曾祖進德，太子中允。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Jinde was Principal of the Crown Prince's Court.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Jinde served as principal of the crown prince's court.

sentences.zh: 祖珍玉，昌明令。

translations.literal: His grandfather Zhenyu was Magistrate of Changming.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Zhenyu was magistrate of Changming.

sentences.zh: 父震，雅州別駕。

translations.literal: His father Zhen was Vice Prefect of Yazhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhen was vice prefect of Yazhou.

sentences.zh: 世寓於荊州之石首。

translations.literal: For generations the family sojourned at Shishou in Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: For generations the family lived at Shishou in Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 遜登進士第，辟襄陽掌書記。

translations.literal: Xun passed the jinshi examination and was appointed chief secretary at Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Xun passed the jinshi examination and was appointed chief secretary at Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 復從事於湖南，主其留務，頗有聲績，累拜池、濠二州刺史。

translations.literal: He again served on the staff of Hunan, managing its resident affairs, and won considerable renown; he was repeatedly promoted to Prefect of the two prefectures of Chi and Hao.
translations.idiomatic: He later served on the Hunan staff, managing affairs in the commander's absence, and earned a strong reputation; he was promoted in succession to prefect of Chi and Hao.

sentences.zh: 先是，濠州之都將楊騰，削刻士卒，州兵三千人謀殺騰。

translations.literal: Previously, Yang Teng, the commanding general of Haozhou, exploited and cheated the soldiers; three thousand troops of the prefecture plotted to kill Teng.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Yang Teng, the garrison commander of Haozhou, had squeezed the troops so hard that three thousand local soldiers plotted to kill him.

sentences.zh: 騰覺之，走揚州，家屬皆死。

translations.literal: Teng sensed it, fled to Yangzhou, and his entire household perished.
translations.idiomatic: Teng discovered the plot, fled to Yangzhou, and his whole family was killed.

sentences.zh: 濠兵不自戢，因行攘剽。

translations.literal: The Hao troops could not restrain themselves and went about looting.
translations.idiomatic: The Haozhou soldiers could not be controlled and turned to plunder.

sentences.zh: 及遜至郡，余亂未殄。

translations.literal: When Xun reached the prefecture, the remaining unrest had not yet been quelled.
translations.idiomatic: By the time Xun arrived, the unrest had not yet been fully suppressed.

sentences.zh: 徐驅其間，為陳逆順利害之勢，眾皆釋甲請罪，因以寧息。

translations.literal: He slowly rode among them, explaining the force of right and wrong and the balance of advantage and harm; all laid down their arms and begged pardon, and thus peace was restored.
translations.idiomatic: He rode calmly among them, explaining what rebellion would cost and what submission would gain; the men laid down their arms and asked forgiveness, and order returned.

sentences.zh: 觀察使旨限外征役，皆不從。

translations.literal: He refused to comply with any corvee or levy beyond the limits set by the military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He refused every requisition for labor or supplies that exceeded the limits set by the military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 入拜虞部郎中。

translations.literal: He entered the capital and was appointed Director of the Ministry of Revenues.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court and was appointed director of the ministry of revenues.

sentences.zh: 元和初，出為衢州刺史。

translations.literal: In the early Yuanhe era he went out as Prefect of Quzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Yuanhe period he was sent out as prefect of Quzhou.

sentences.zh: 以政績殊尤，遷越州刺史，兼御史大夫、浙東都團練觀察使。

translations.literal: For outstanding administrative achievements he was promoted to Prefect of Yuezhou, concurrently Grand Censor and Military Training Commissioner and Military Commissioner of Zhedong.
translations.idiomatic: For exceptional performance he was promoted to prefect of Yuezhou, grand censor, and military training and observation commissioner of Zhedong.

sentences.zh: 先是，貞元初，皇甫政鎮浙東，嘗福建兵亂，逐觀察使吳詵。

translations.literal: Previously, in the early Zhenyuan era, Huangfu Zheng commanded Zhedong; at one time Fujian troops mutinied and drove out Military Commissioner Wu Shen.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, in the early Zhenyuan era, Huangfu Zheng governed Zhedong; when Fujian troops mutinied they expelled military commissioner Wu Shen.

sentences.zh: 政以所鎮實壓閩境，請權益兵三千，俟賊平而罷。

translations.literal: Zheng, since his command actually bordered Fujian territory, requested permission to augment his forces by three thousand men, to be disbanded once the rebels were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Because his circuit bordered Fujian, Zheng asked to raise three thousand extra troops temporarily until the rebellion ended.

sentences.zh: 賊平向三十年，而所益兵仍舊。

translations.literal: Nearly thirty years after the rebels were pacified, the augmented troops remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: Nearly thirty years after the rebellion was crushed, those extra troops were still on the rolls.

sentences.zh: 遜視事數日，舉奏停之。

translations.literal: Within days of assuming office Xun memorialized and had them discontinued.
translations.idiomatic: Within days of taking office Xun memorialized to abolish them.

sentences.zh: 遜為政以均一貧富、扶弱抑強為己任，故所至稱理。

translations.literal: Xun governed with equalizing rich and poor and supporting the weak while restraining the strong as his personal charge; therefore wherever he went he was praised for good governance.
translations.idiomatic: Xun made it his mission to level the gap between rich and poor and protect the weak against the strong, and wherever he served he won praise for good government.

sentences.zh: 九年，入為給事中。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he entered the capital as Chief of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he entered court as chief of the imperial secretariat.

sentences.zh: 遜以舊制只日視事對群臣，遜奏論曰：「事君之義，有犯無隱。

translations.literal: Xun, noting that by old regulation the emperor reviewed affairs and received the ministers only on designated days, memorialized, saying: "The duty of serving one's lord is to speak out even when it means offense, not to conceal.
translations.idiomatic: Because the old rule allowed the emperor to receive ministers only on fixed audience days, Xun memorialized: "Serving a ruler means speaking up even at the risk of giving offense.

sentences.zh: 陳誠啟沃，不必擇辰。

translations.literal: To present sincere counsel and provide nourishing guidance, one need not choose a particular day.
translations.idiomatic: Honest counsel and timely remonstrance should not have to wait for a chosen day.

sentences.zh: 今群臣敷奏，乃候只日，是畢歲臣下睹天顏、獻可否能幾何？」

translations.literal: Now when ministers present memorials they must wait for the designated day—how often in a whole year can officials below behold the imperial countenance and offer approval or rejection?"
translations.idiomatic: Now officials must wait for audience day to speak—how many times in a year can the court actually see the emperor's face and debate what should be done?"

sentences.zh: 憲宗嘉之，乃許不擇時奏對。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzong approved this and permitted memorials and audiences without regard to fixed times.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzong approved the proposal and allowed memorials and audiences at any time.

sentences.zh: 俄遷戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Vice Minister of the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was promoted to vice minister of the ministry of revenue.

sentences.zh: 元和十年，拜襄州刺史，充山南東道節度、觀察等使。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Yuanhe he was appointed Prefect of Xiangzhou and commissioned as Military Commissioner and Military Commissioner of the Shan'nan East Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Yuanhe he was appointed prefect of Xiangzhou and military commissioner of the Shan'nan East circuit.

sentences.zh: 襄陽前領八郡，唐、鄧、隋在焉。

translations.literal: Xiangyang had previously administered eight prefectures, among them Tang, Deng, and Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangyang had formerly overseen eight prefectures, including Tang, Deng, and Sui.

sentences.zh: 是時方討吳元濟，朝議以唐、蔡鄰接，遂以鄧隸唐州，三郡別為節制，命高霞寓領之，專俟攻討。

translations.literal: At that time the court was campaigning against Wu Yuanji; the court deliberated that Tang and Cai prefectures bordered each other, so Deng was subordinated to Tangzhou and the three prefectures were placed under separate command, with Gao Xiayu appointed to lead them devoted solely to the attack.
translations.idiomatic: The court was then campaigning against Wu Yuanji; because Tang and Cai bordered each other, Deng was placed under Tangzhou, the three prefectures were given their own command, and Gao Xiayu was put in charge solely to conduct the offensive.

sentences.zh: 遜以五州賦餉之。

translations.literal: Xun supplied them from the tax revenues of five prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Xun supplied their provisions from the tax revenues of five prefectures.

sentences.zh: 時孫代嚴綬鎮襄陽。

translations.literal: At that time Xun replaced Yan Shou in commanding Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Xun replaced Yan Shou as military commissioner of Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 綬以八州兵討賊在唐州。

translations.literal: Shou led the troops of eight prefectures to suppress the bandits while stationed at Tang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Shou commanded the armies of eight prefectures against the rebels from his base at Tang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 既而綬以無功罷兵柄，命高霞寓代綬將兵於唐州，其襄陽軍隸於霞寓。

translations.literal: Before long Shou was stripped of military command for achieving no merit; Gao Xiayu was ordered to replace Shou in commanding troops at Tang Prefecture, and the Xiangyang army was placed under Xiayu's command.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Shou was removed from command for lack of results. Gao Xiayu was appointed to replace him at Tang Prefecture, and the Xiangyang force was subordinated to Xiayu.

sentences.zh: 軍士家口在襄州者，遜厚撫之，士卒多舍霞寓亡歸。

translations.literal: As for soldiers whose families were in Xiang Prefecture, Xun treated them generously; many troops abandoned Xiayu and fled back to him.
translations.idiomatic: Xun treated soldiers whose families lived in Xiang Prefecture with generous care, and many troops deserted Xiayu to rejoin him.

sentences.zh: 既而霞寓為賊所敗，乃移過於遜，言供饋不時。

translations.literal: Before long Xiayu was defeated by the bandits; he then shifted the blame onto Xun, saying that supplies had not been delivered on time.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiayu was defeated by the rebels, he blamed Xun, claiming that provisions had arrived late.

sentences.zh: 霞寓本出禁軍，內官皆佐之。

translations.literal: Xiayu had originally come from the imperial guard, and eunuch officials all assisted him.
translations.idiomatic: Xiayu was a veteran of the imperial guard, and eunuch officials all served at his side.

sentences.zh: 既貶官，中人皆言遜撓霞寓軍，所以致敗。

translations.literal: After he was demoted, the eunuchs all said that Xun had undermined Xiayu's army and thus brought about the defeat.
translations.idiomatic: After Xun was demoted, the eunuchs all claimed he had sabotaged Xiayu's campaign and caused the defeat.

sentences.zh: 上令中使至襄州聽察曲直，奏言遜不直，乃左授太子賓客分司，又降為恩王傅。

translations.literal: The emperor sent palace envoys to Xiang Prefecture to investigate right and wrong; they reported that Xun was in the wrong, so he was transferred leftward to be an Honored Guest of the Heir Apparent with concurrent service, and further reduced to tutor of the Prince of En.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor dispatched palace envoys to Xiang Prefecture to determine who was at fault. They reported against Xun, and he was demoted to Honored Guest of the Heir Apparent in concurrent service, then reduced again to tutor of the Prince of En.

sentences.zh: 十三年，李師道效順，命遜為左散騎常侍，馳赴東平諭之。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, Li Shidao expressed willingness to submit; Xun was appointed Left Regular Attendant of the Palace Secretariat and sent posthaste to Dongping to instruct him.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of the reign, Li Shidao offered his submission. Xun was appointed Left Regular Attendant of the Palace Secretariat and dispatched at speed to Dongping to win him over.

sentences.zh: 師道得詔意動，即請效順，旋為其下所惑而止。

translations.literal: Shidao, upon receiving the edict, was moved in heart and immediately requested to submit, but was soon swayed by his subordinates and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Shidao was moved by the imperial message and at once offered to surrender, but his subordinates soon talked him out of it.

sentences.zh: 遜還，未幾，除京兆尹，改國子祭酒。

translations.literal: Xun returned, and before long was appointed Prefect of the Capital District, then changed to Chancellor of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Xun returned to court and was soon made Prefect of the Capital District, then Chancellor of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 十四年，拜許州刺史，充忠武節度、陳許溵蔡等州觀察處置等使。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he was appointed Prefect of Xuzhou and commissioned as Military Commissioner of Zhongwu and Military Commissioner of Chen, Xu, Wen, and Cai prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he was appointed Prefect of Xuzhou and commissioned as Military Commissioner of Zhongwu with oversight of Chen, Xu, Wen, and Cai prefectures.

sentences.zh: 是時，新罹兵戰，難遽完緝。

translations.literal: At that time the region had newly suffered warfare and could not quickly be fully restored.
translations.idiomatic: The region had just been ravaged by war and could not be put in order overnight.

sentences.zh: 及遜至，集大軍與之約束，嚴具示賞罰必信，號令數百言，士皆感悅。

translations.literal: When Xun arrived, he gathered the main army and imposed regulations on them, strictly displaying that rewards and punishments would surely be carried out; his orders ran to several hundred words, and the soldiers were all moved and pleased.
translations.idiomatic: When Xun arrived, he assembled the main force, laid down strict rules, and made it plain that rewards and punishments would be enforced without fail. His proclamation ran to several hundred words, and the troops were deeply impressed.

sentences.zh: 長慶元年，幽、鎮繼亂。

translations.literal: In the first year of Changqing, Youzhou and Zhenzhou rebelled in succession.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Changqing, the circuits of Youzhou and Zhenzhou rebelled in turn.

sentences.zh: 遜請身先討賊，不許。

translations.literal: Xun requested to take the lead in attacking the rebels; permission was denied.
translations.idiomatic: Xun asked to lead the campaign personally, but the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 但命以兵一萬，會於行營。

translations.literal: He was only ordered to send ten thousand troops to rendezvous at the field headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered instead to dispatch ten thousand troops to join the field headquarters.

sentences.zh: 遜奉詔，即日發兵，故先諸軍而至，由是進位檢校吏部尚書。

translations.literal: Xun obeyed the edict and mobilized troops that same day; therefore he arrived before the other armies and was promoted to Acting Minister of the Ministry of Civil Office.
translations.idiomatic: Xun obeyed at once and marched his troops out the same day, arriving ahead of the other armies. For this he was promoted to acting minister of civil appointments.

sentences.zh: 尋改鳳翔節度使，行至京師，以疾陳乞，改刑部尚書。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Military Commissioner of Fengxiang; when he reached the capital he pleaded illness and was changed to Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to military commissioner of Fengxiang, but upon reaching the capital he pleaded illness and was reassigned as minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 長慶三年正月卒，年六十三，廢朝一日，贈右僕射。

translations.literal: In the first month of the third year of Changqing he died, aged sixty-three; court mourning was suspended for one day, and he was posthumously granted the right vice grand councilor.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the first month of the third year of Changqing, aged sixty-three. Court audiences were suspended for one day, and he was posthumously granted right vice grand councilor.

sentences.zh: 遜幼孤，寓居江陵。

translations.literal: Xun was orphaned in youth and lived in Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: Xun lost his parents young and grew up in Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 與其弟建，皆安貧苦，易衣並食，講習不倦。

translations.literal: He and his younger brother Jian both endured poverty, sharing clothes and food, studying without weariness.
translations.idiomatic: He and his younger brother Jian lived in poverty together, sharing clothes and meals and studying without rest.

sentences.zh: 遜兄造，知二弟賢，日為營丐，成其誌業。

translations.literal: Xun's elder brother Zao, knowing both younger brothers were worthy, daily worked to support them by begging and fulfilled their aspirations for learning.
translations.idiomatic: Their elder brother Zao, recognizing both younger brothers' talent, begged daily to support them and see them through their studies.

sentences.zh: 建先遜一年卒。

translations.literal: Jian died one year before Xun.
translations.idiomatic: Jian died one year before Xun did.

sentences.zh: 兄弟同致休顯，士君子多之。

translations.literal: The brothers together attained honor and eminence; scholar-gentlemen greatly admired them.
translations.idiomatic: The brothers rose together to distinction, and men of learning held them in high regard.

sentences.zh: 謚曰恭肅。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Gongsu.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously titled Gongsu, Reverent and Solemn.

sentences.zh: 造早卒。

translations.literal: Zao died early.
translations.idiomatic: Zao died young.

sentences.zh: 建，字杓直，家素清貧，無舊業。

translations.literal: Jian, courtesy name Shaozhi, came from a family that had long been poor and had no inherited estate.
translations.idiomatic: Jian, courtesy name Shaozhi, was born into a family of longstanding poverty with no ancestral property.

sentences.zh: 與兄造、遜於荊南躬耕致養，嗜學力文。

translations.literal: With his elder brothers Zao and Xun he personally farmed in Jingnan to support their parents, and he loved learning and worked at writing.
translations.idiomatic: Together with his elder brothers Zao and Xun he farmed in southern Jing to support the household, devoted to study and literary work.

sentences.zh: 舉進士，選授秘書省校書郎。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and was selected and appointed Proofreader in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and was appointed a proofreader in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 德宗聞其名，用為右拾遺、翰林學士。

translations.literal: Emperor Dezong heard his name and appointed him Right Reminder and Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Dezong heard of him and appointed him Right Reminder and Hanlin Academician.

sentences.zh: 元和六年，坐事罷職，降詹事府司直。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Yuanhe he was dismissed from office for an offense and demoted to Direct Clerk in the Household of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Yuanhe he was dismissed for an offense and demoted to Direct Clerk in the Household of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 高郢為御史大夫，奏為殿中侍御史，遷兵部郎中、知制誥。

translations.literal: Gao Ying was Censor-in-Chief; he memorialized to appoint Jian Palace Censor, then transferred him to Director in the Ministry of War with charge of drafting edicts.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Ying served as Censor-in-Chief, he recommended Jian as Palace Censor; Jian was later promoted to Director in the Ministry of War with responsibility for drafting edicts.

sentences.zh: 自以草詔思遲，不願司文翰，改京兆尹。

translations.literal: He considered himself slow in composing edicts and did not wish to handle literary duties, so he was changed to Prefect of the Capital District.
translations.idiomatic: Finding himself slow at drafting edicts, he asked to leave literary duties and was appointed Prefect of the Capital District.

sentences.zh: 與宰相韋貫之友善。

translations.literal: He was on friendly terms with the chancellor Wei Guanzhi.
translations.idiomatic: He was close friends with the chancellor Wei Guanzhi.

sentences.zh: 貫之罷相，建亦出為澧州刺史。

translations.literal: When Guanzhi was removed as chancellor, Jian was also sent out as Prefect of Li Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Guanzhi lost the chancellorship, Jian was sent out as Prefect of Li Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 征拜太常少卿，尋以本官知禮部貢舉。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed Vice Minister of Rites, and soon in that same office he was put in charge of the Ministry of Rites examinations.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as Vice Minister of Rites and soon given charge of the civil service examinations.

sentences.zh: 建取舍非其人，又惑於請托，故其年選士不精，坐罰俸料。

translations.literal: Jian's selections were not the right men, and he was also misled by solicitations; therefore that year's chosen scholars were not well chosen, and he was punished by deduction of salary.
translations.idiomatic: Jian selected unworthy candidates and was swayed by patronage, so that year's examination picks were poor, and his salary was docked as punishment.

sentences.zh: 明年，除禮部侍郎，竟以人情不洽，改為刑部。

translations.literal: The next year he was appointed Vice Minister of Rites, but in the end, because relations with colleagues were not harmonious, he was changed to the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was made Vice Minister of Rites, but poor relations with colleagues led to his transfer to the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 建名位雖顯，以廉儉自處，家不理垣屋，士友推之。

translations.literal: Though Jian's fame and rank were prominent, he maintained himself in integrity and frugality; at home he did not repair walls and roofs, and scholar-friends praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Though Jian rose to high rank, he lived with integrity and thrift, never repairing his house, and his peers held him in esteem.

sentences.zh: 長慶二年二月卒，贈工部尚書。

translations.literal: In the second month of the second year of Changqing he died; posthumously he was given Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the second month of the second year of Changqing and was posthumously granted the title Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 三子：訥、恪、樸。

translations.literal: Three sons: Ne, Ke, and Pu.
translations.idiomatic: He had three sons: Ne, Ke, and Pu.

sentences.zh: 訥最知名，官至華州刺史、檢校尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: Ne was the most renowned; he reached Prefect of Hua Prefecture and Acting Minister of the Right.
translations.idiomatic: Ne was the most famous; he rose to Prefect of Hua Prefecture and Acting Minister of the Right.

sentences.zh: 薛戎，字元夫，河中寶鼎人。

translations.literal: Xue Rong, courtesy name Yuanfu, was a native of Baoding in Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Rong, courtesy name Yuanfu, was a native of Baoding in Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 少有學術，不求聞達，居於毗陵之陽羨山。

translations.literal: In youth he had learning, sought no fame or advancement, and lived on Yangxian Mountain in Piling.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man he was deeply learned but sought no fame, living on Yangxian Mountain in Piling.

sentences.zh: 年余四十，不易其操。

translations.literal: Past forty years of age, he did not change his conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Even past forty he never changed his way of life.

sentences.zh: 江西觀察使李衡辟為從事，使者三返方應。

translations.literal: Li Heng, Military Commissioner of Jiangxi, recruited him as an aide; the envoy returned three times before he consented.
translations.idiomatic: Li Heng, Military Commissioner of Jiangxi, invited him to serve as an aide; only after the envoy came back three times did he agree.

sentences.zh: 故相齊映代衡，又留署職，府罷歸山。

translations.literal: The former chancellor Qi Ying replaced Heng and also retained him in office; when the office closed he returned to the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: When the former chancellor Qi Ying replaced Heng, he kept Rong on staff; when that appointment ended, Rong went back to his mountain retreat.

sentences.zh: 福建觀察使柳冕表為從事，累月，轉殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: Liu Mian, Military Commissioner of Fujian, memorialized to appoint him as an aide; after several months he was transferred to Palace Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Mian, Military Commissioner of Fujian, recommended him as an aide; within months he was promoted to Palace Censor.

sentences.zh: 會泉州闕刺史，冕署戎權領州事。

translations.literal: It happened that Quan Prefecture lacked a prefect; Mian appointed Rong to administer the prefecture on a provisional basis.
translations.idiomatic: When Quan Prefecture had no prefect, Mian put Rong in temporary charge of its affairs.

sentences.zh: 是時，姚南仲節制鄭滑，從事馬總以其道直為監軍使誣奏，貶泉州別駕。

translations.literal: At that time Yao Nanzhong commanded Zheng and Hua; the aide Ma Zong, because his conduct was upright, was falsely denounced by the army supervisor and demoted to Vice-Prefect of Quan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Yao Nanzhong commanded Zheng and Hua circuits. Ma Zong, an aide noted for his integrity, was falsely accused by the army supervisor and demoted to Vice-Prefect of Quan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 冕附會權勢，欲構成總罪，使戎按問曲成之。

translations.literal: Mian curried favor with the powerful and wished to fabricate charges against Zong, having Rong conduct the investigation and frame the case.
translations.idiomatic: Mian courted the powerful and sought to frame Zong, ordering Rong to investigate and manufacture the case against him.

sentences.zh: 戎以總無辜，不從冕意，別白其狀。

translations.literal: Rong held that Zong was innocent, did not follow Mian's intent, and separately submitted a clear report of the facts.
translations.idiomatic: Rong believed Zong was innocent, refused to go along with Mian, and filed a separate memorial stating the truth.

sentences.zh: 戎還自泉州，冕盛氣據衙而見賓客。

translations.literal: When Rong returned from Quan Prefecture, Mian received guests in the yamen with fierce bearing.
translations.idiomatic: When Rong returned from Quan Prefecture, Mian sat in his office in a towering rage to receive visitors.

sentences.zh: 戎遂歷東廂從容而入。

translations.literal: Rong then entered at leisure through the east wing.
translations.idiomatic: Rong walked in unhurried through the east corridor.

sentences.zh: 冕度勢未可屈，徐起以見，一揖而退。

translations.literal: Mian gauged that the situation could not be forced to yield; he slowly rose to receive him, gave one bow, and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing he could not intimidate Rong, Mian rose slowly to greet him, exchanged a single bow, and let him go.

sentences.zh: 又構其罪以狀聞，置戎於佛寺，環以武夫，恣其侵辱，如是累月，誘令成總之罪。

translations.literal: He again fabricated charges against him and reported them in a memorial, confined Rong in a Buddhist temple surrounded by armed men, allowing them to insult him at will for months on end, trying to induce him to confirm Zong's guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Mian then fabricated new charges and reported them to the throne, confined Rong in a Buddhist temple ringed with armed men, and for months allowed them to abuse him at will, trying to force him to validate the case against Zong.

sentences.zh: 操心如一，竟不動搖。

translations.literal: His heart and conduct remained consistent; in the end he did not waver.
translations.idiomatic: Rong's resolve never changed; in the end he did not yield.

sentences.zh: 杜佑鎮淮南，知戎之冤，乃上其表，發書諭冕，戎難方解，遂辭職寓居於江湖間。

translations.literal: Du You commanded Huainan, knew of Rong's injustice, and submitted his memorial; he sent a letter instructing Mian, and only then was Rong's ordeal resolved; he then resigned and lived in retirement along the rivers and lakes.
translations.idiomatic: Du You, commanding Huainan, learned of Rong's wrongful treatment, forwarded his memorial, and wrote to Mian to intervene. Only then was Rong released; he resigned and lived in seclusion on the waterways.

sentences.zh: 後閻濟美為福建觀察使，備聞其事，奏充副使。

translations.literal: Later Yan Jimei was Military Commissioner of Fujian; having fully heard of the affair, he memorialized to appoint Rong Deputy Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Yan Jimei became Military Commissioner of Fujian, he heard the full story and recommended Rong as deputy commissioner.

sentences.zh: 又隨濟美移鎮浙東，改侍御史，入拜刑部員外郎。

translations.literal: He again followed Jimei when he transferred to command Zhedong, was changed to Attending Censor, and entered court as Vice Director in the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Jimei to Zhedong, was promoted to Attending Censor, and then entered the capital as Vice Director in the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 出為河南令，累改衢、湖、常三州刺史，遷浙東觀察使。

translations.literal: He went out as Magistrate of Henan, successively changed to Prefect of Qu, Hu, and Chang prefectures, and was promoted to Military Commissioner of Zhedong.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Magistrate of Henan, then as prefect of Qu, Hu, and Chang in succession, and was finally promoted to Military Commissioner of Zhedong.

sentences.zh: 所蒞皆以政績聞。

translations.literal: Everywhere he served he was known for administrative achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he served, his governance won renown.

sentences.zh: 居數歲，以疾辭官。

translations.literal: After several years he resigned on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: After several years he retired because of illness.

sentences.zh: 長慶元年十月卒，贈左散騎常侍。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the first year of Changqing he died; posthumously he was given Left Regular Attendant of the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the tenth month of the first year of Changqing and was posthumously granted Left Regular Attendant of the Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 戎檢身處約，不務虛名。

translations.literal: Rong restrained himself and lived simply, not pursuing empty reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Rong lived with strict self-discipline and modest means, caring nothing for hollow fame.

sentences.zh: 俸入之余，散於宗族。

translations.literal: What remained of his salary he distributed among his clan.
translations.idiomatic: He gave whatever salary he did not need to his extended family.

sentences.zh: 身歿之後，人無譏焉。

translations.literal: After his death no one spoke ill of him.
translations.idiomatic: After his death no one had a word of reproach for him.

sentences.zh: 兄弟五人，季弟放最知名。

translations.literal: Among five brothers, the youngest brother Fang was the most renowned.
translations.idiomatic: He had five brothers; the youngest, Fang, was the most famous.

sentences.zh: 放登進士第，性端厚寡言，於是非不甚系意。

translations.literal: Fang passed the jinshi examination; his nature was upright and generous and sparing of speech, and he did not greatly fix his mind on right and wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Fang passed the jinshi examination. Steadfast and taciturn by nature, he did not fuss over every dispute of right and wrong.

sentences.zh: 累佐籓府，蒞事幹敏。

translations.literal: He repeatedly served in regional headquarters and was quick and capable in handling affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He served repeatedly in regional administrations and proved swift and competent in office.

sentences.zh: 官至試大理評事，擢拜右拾遺，轉補闕，歷水部、兵部二員外，遷兵部郎中。

translations.literal: He reached Acting Evaluator of the Court of Judicial Review, was promoted to Right Reminder, transferred to Supplementation Censor, served as Vice Director in the Ministries of Works and War in succession, and was promoted to Director in the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Acting Evaluator of the Court of Judicial Review, then Right Reminder, Supplementation Censor, Vice Director in the Ministries of Works and War in turn, and finally Director in the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 遇憲宗以儲皇好書，求端士輔導經義，選充皇太子侍讀。

translations.literal: It happened that Emperor Xianzong, because the heir apparent loved books, sought upright scholars to guide him in the classics; Fang was selected to serve as Reader to the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xianzong, finding the crown prince fond of learning, sought upright scholars to instruct him in the classics, Fang was chosen as Reader to the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 及穆宗嗣位，未聽政間，放多在左右，密參機命。

translations.literal: When Emperor Muzong succeeded to the throne, during the interval before he took up governance Fang was often at his side, secretly participating in confidential decisions.
translations.idiomatic: When Muzong succeeded to the throne, Fang was often at his side during the period before he formally assumed rule, quietly advising on weighty matters.

sentences.zh: 穆宗常謂放曰：「小子初承大寶，懼不克荷，先生宜為相，以匡不逮。」

translations.literal: Emperor Muzong often said to Fang: "I, a young man, have newly assumed the great inheritance and fear I cannot bear it. You, sir, ought to become chancellor to help where I fall short."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Muzong often told Fang, "I have just taken up the throne and fear I am not equal to the burden. You, sir, should serve as chancellor and guide me where I fall short."

sentences.zh: 放叩頭曰：「臣實庸淺，獲侍冕旒，固不足猥塵大位。

translations.literal: Fang kowtowed and said: "Your servant is truly mediocre and shallow; that I have been allowed to attend Your Majesty is already too much—I am surely not fit to sully so high an office.
translations.idiomatic: Fang kowtowed and said, "Your servant is truly unworthy. That I may attend Your Majesty is honor enough; I am surely not fit to defile so exalted a post.

sentences.zh: 輔弼之任，自有賢能。」

translations.literal: The task of assisting and supporting falls to men of talent and ability."
translations.idiomatic: The work of governing belongs to those who truly have talent."

sentences.zh: 其言無矯飾，皆此類也。

translations.literal: His words were without affected ornament—all were of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: He never spoke with artifice; this was typical of him.

sentences.zh: 穆宗深嘉其誠，因召對思政殿，賜以金紫之服。

translations.literal: Emperor Muzong deeply admired his sincerity; he therefore summoned him for audience in the Hall of Contemplating Governance and bestowed on him robes of gold and purple.
translations.idiomatic: Muzong deeply valued his sincerity, summoned him to the Hall of Contemplating Governance, and granted him gold-and-purple robes of rank.

sentences.zh: 轉工部侍郎、集賢學士。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Minister of Works and Academician of the Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice Minister of Works and Academician of the Academy.

sentences.zh: 雖任非峻切，而恩顧轉隆。

translations.literal: Though his office was not the most exalted, imperial favor toward him grew ever greater.
translations.idiomatic: Though his post was not the highest, the emperor's favor toward him steadily increased.

sentences.zh: 轉刑部侍郎，職如故。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Minister of Justice; his duties remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Vice Minister of Justice while retaining his previous duties.

sentences.zh: 穆宗常謂侍臣曰：「朕欲習學經史，何先？」

translations.literal: Emperor Muzong often said to his attending ministers: "I wish to study the classics and histories—where should I begin?"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Muzong often asked his ministers, "I wish to study the classics and histories. Where should I begin?"

sentences.zh: 放對曰：「經者，先聖之至言，仲尼之所發明，皆天人之極致，誠萬代不刊之典也。

translations.literal: Fang replied: "The classics are the supreme words of the former sages, elucidated by Confucius—they are the utmost of Heaven and man, truly canons unaltered for ten thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: Fang answered, "The classics are the supreme teachings of the sages, expounded by Confucius. They express the highest truths of Heaven and humanity and are standards for all ages.

sentences.zh: 史記前代成敗得失之跡，亦足鑒其興亡。

translations.literal: Historical records preserve the traces of success and failure, gain and loss in former ages, and are also sufficient to mirror rise and fall.
translations.idiomatic: Histories record the successes and failures of past ages and can serve as mirrors of rise and fall.

sentences.zh: 然得失相參，是非無準的，固不可為經典比也。」

translations.literal: Yet gain and loss are mixed together and right and wrong have no fixed standard; they truly cannot be compared with the classics."
translations.idiomatic: But they mingle success with failure and offer no fixed standard of judgment, so they cannot be put on a par with the classics."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「《六經》所尚不一，誌學之士，白首不能盡通，如何得其要？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "The Six Classics each emphasize different things; scholars who aspire to learning cannot fully master them even with white hair—how can one grasp their essentials?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "The Six Classics each stress different things. A devoted student may study until his hair turns white without mastering them all. How can one grasp what matters most?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「《論語》者《六經》之菁華，《孝經》者人倫之本。

translations.literal: He replied: "The Analects is the essence of the Six Classics; the Classic of Filial Piety is the root of human relations.
translations.idiomatic: Fang replied, "The Analects is the flower of the Six Classics, and the Classic of Filial Piety is the foundation of human relations.

sentences.zh: 窮理執要，真可謂聖人至言。

translations.literal: To exhaust principle and grasp essentials— these can truly be called the supreme words of the sage.
translations.idiomatic: To penetrate their principles and hold fast to what is essential is to receive the sage's true teaching.

sentences.zh: 是以漢朝《論語》首列學官，光武令虎賁之士皆習《孝經》，玄宗親為《孝經》註解，皆使當時大理，四海乂寧。

translations.literal: Therefore in the Han dynasty the Analects was first listed among the official academies; Emperor Guangwu ordered the Tiger Guard to study the Classic of Filial Piety; Emperor Xuanzong personally annotated the Classic of Filial Piety—all brought great order in their time and peace throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: That is why the Han placed the Analects first among the state academies, why Emperor Guangwu had the Tiger Guard study the Classic of Filial Piety, and why Emperor Xuanzong personally annotated it—each age found great order, and the realm was at peace.

sentences.zh: 蓋人知孝慈，氣感和樂之所致也。」

translations.literal: This is because when people know filial piety and kindness, harmonious feeling and joy are what bring it about."
translations.idiomatic: When people understand filial piety and compassion, harmony and contentment follow naturally."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「聖人以孝為至德要道，其信然乎！」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "The sage took filial piety as the utmost virtue and essential way—is this indeed so!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "The sage held filial piety to be the highest virtue and the essential path—is that not true!"

sentences.zh: 轉兵部侍郎、禮部尚書，判院事。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Minister of the Ministry of War and Minister of Rites, with concurrent direction of the Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He was then promoted to Vice Minister of the Ministry of War and Minister of Rites, with concurrent direction of the Academy.

sentences.zh: 放閨門之內，尤推孝睦，孤孀百口，家貧每不給贍，常苦俸薄。

translations.literal: Within Fang's household he especially practiced filial harmony; more than a hundred widows and orphans depended on him, the family was poor and often could not be fully provided for, and he constantly suffered from thin salary.
translations.idiomatic: At home Fang was especially devoted to filial piety and harmony. More than a hundred widows and orphans relied on him; the household was poor and often went short, and his salary was never enough.

sentences.zh: 放因召對，懇求外任。

translations.literal: Fang therefore requested an outside appointment when summoned for audience.
translations.idiomatic: Fang therefore asked, during an imperial audience, to be sent to a post outside the capital.

sentences.zh: 其時偶以節制無闕，乃授以廉問。

translations.literal: At that time there happened to be no vacant military commissioner post, so he was granted an inspection commission.
translations.idiomatic: No military commissioner post was vacant at the time, so he was given a provincial inspection commission instead.

sentences.zh: 及鎮江西，惟用清潔為理，一方之人，至今思之。

translations.literal: When he governed Jiangxi he governed solely through integrity and clean administration; the people of that region still remember him to this day.
translations.idiomatic: As commissioner of Jiangxi he ruled through integrity alone, and the people there remember him to this day.

sentences.zh: 寶歷元年，卒於江西觀察使，廢朝一日。

translations.literal: In the first year of Baoli he died while serving as Military Commissioner of Jiangxi; the court suspended court for one day.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Baoli he died in office as Military Commissioner of Jiangxi, and the court suspended audience for one day in mourning.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：穆秘監之剛正不奪，如寒松倚巖，千丈勁節。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: Supervisor of the Palace Library Mu's uncompromising uprightness was like a cold pine leaning against a cliff—thousands of feet of sturdy joints.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer writes: Supervisor of the Palace Library Mu's inflexible integrity stood like a pine on a cliff, unyielding for a thousand feet.

sentences.zh: 而竇容州之敢決，如鷙鳥逐雀，英氣動人，巖穴之流，罕能及此。

translations.literal: As for Prefect of Rongzhou Dou's bold decisiveness, it was like a fierce bird chasing sparrows—heroic spirit stirring men; hermits and recluses could rarely match this.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect of Rongzhou Dou's daring resolve was like a hawk striking at sparrows—bold spirit that stirred all who saw it. Recluses in mountain caves could seldom measure up.

sentences.zh: 然矯激過當，君子不為。

translations.literal: Yet excessive straining and provocation—gentlemen do not do this.
translations.idiomatic: Yet to go too far in harsh rectitude is something a true gentleman would not do.

sentences.zh: 如塤如篪，不通不介，士行之美，崔氏諸子有焉。

translations.literal: Like xun and chi in harmony, neither obstinate nor aloof—the beauty of gentlemen's conduct, the sons of the Cui family possessed it.
translations.idiomatic: Harmonious as paired flutes, firm yet not rigid—the Cui brothers embodied the finest qualities of a scholar-official.

sentences.zh: 建、遜之貞方，戎、放之道義，元和已來，稱為令族，宜哉！

translations.literal: Jian and Xun's integrity and rectitude, Rong and Fang's moral principle—from Yuanhe onward they were called an eminent clan; rightly so!
translations.idiomatic: Jian and Xun's steadfast character, Rong and Fang's moral conduct—from the Yuanhe era onward their families were hailed as model clans, and with good reason.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：穆之贊、質，竇之常、群，跡參時傑，氣爽人文。

translations.literal: In praise: Mu's Zan and Zhi, Dou's Chang and Qun—their tracks joined the era's finest men, their spirit refreshing human culture.
translations.idiomatic: In praise: Mu Zan and Mu Zhi, Dou Chang and Dou Qun—their careers placed them among the age's leading figures, their spirit enlivening the culture of their time.

sentences.zh: 二李英英，四崔濟濟。

translations.literal: The two Lis, splendid; the four Cuis, abundant.
translations.idiomatic: The two Li brothers, shining in eminence; the four Cui brothers, flourishing in number and talent.

sentences.zh: 薛氏三門，難兄難弟。

translations.literal: The three families of the Xue clan—brothers each as worthy as the other.
translations.idiomatic: Across the three branches of the Xue family, every brother was the equal of the next.
